source: Bhagavad Gita 1.1 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The King Dhritarashtra asked, "O Sanjaya! What happened on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra when my people and the Pandavas gathered?"
sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच / धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः। / मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.2 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Sanjaya replied: "When Prince Duryodhana saw the Pandavas' army paraded, he approached his preceptor Guru Drona and spoke these words:
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा। / आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.3 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Revered Father! Behold this mighty host of the Pandavas, paraded by the son of King Drupada, your wise disciple.
sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्। / व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.4 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: In it are heroes and great bowmen; the equals in battle of Arjuna, Bheema, Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada—all great soldiers.
sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि। / युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.5 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitan, the valiant king of Benares, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya—a master of many.
sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्। / पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.6 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Yudhamanyu, Uttamouja, Soubhadra, and the sons of Droupadi—all famous men.
sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्। / सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.7 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: No changes needed.
sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम। / नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.8 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: You come first; then Bheeshma, Karna, Kripa, great warriors; Ashwaththama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadhatta;
sanskrit: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः। / अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.9 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And many others, all ready to die for My sake; all armed, all skilled in warfare.
sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः। / नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.10 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Yet our army seems weaker, though commanded by Bhishma; their army seems stronger, though commanded by Bhima.
sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्। / पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.11 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Therefore, let the rank and file stand firm in their posts according to battalions, and all you generals around Bheeshma.
sanskrit: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः। / भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.12 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Then, to enliven his spirits, the brave Grandfather Bheeshma, the eldest of the Kuru clan, blew his conch, its sound resembling that of a lion's roar.
sanskrit: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः। / सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.13 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And immediately, all the conches, drums, trumpets, and horns blared forth in a tumultuous uproar.
sanskrit: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः। / सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.14 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Then, seated in their spacious war chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their divine conch shells.
sanskrit: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ। / माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.15 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya, and Arjuna blew his Devadatta; brave Bheema blew his renowned shell, Poundra.
sanskrit: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः। / पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.16 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, Nakula, and Sahadeva, the Sughosa and Manipushpaka, respectively.
sanskrit: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। / नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.17 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And the Maharaja of Benares, the great archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier, Dhrishtayumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the invincible one,
sanskrit: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः। / धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.18 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And, O King! Drupada's sons, Droupadi's sons, and the great soldier Soubhadra blew their conches.
sanskrit: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते। / सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.19 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, shaking heaven and earth with its echoing violence.
sanskrit: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्। / नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.20 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Then, upon beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the battlefield, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose flag bore the image of Hanuman,
sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः। / प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.21 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Raising his bow, he spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible Lord of the earth! Please draw up my chariot between the two armies.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते। / सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.22 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: So that I may observe those who must fight on my side and those who must fight against me.
sanskrit: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्। / कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.23 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And gaze upon this array of soldiers, eager to please the sons of Dhritarashtra who are sinful.
sanskrit: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः। / धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.24 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Sanjaya said: "Having listened to Arjuna's request, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His bright chariot in the midst between the two armies.
sanskrit: संजय उवाच / एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत। / सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.25 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Where Bheeshma and Drona had led all the rulers of the earth, they spoke thus: O Arjuna! Behold, these members of the family of Kuru are assembled.
sanskrit: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्। / उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.26 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: There, Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, and friends.
sanskrit: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान्। / आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.27 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Fathers-in-law and benefactors were arrayed on both sides, and Arjuna then gazed at all those kinsmen before him.
sanskrit: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि। / तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.28 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: And his heart melted with pity, and sadly he spoke: "O my Lord! When I see all these, my own people, thirsting for battle,
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्। / दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.29 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: My limbs are failing me, my throat is parched, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.
sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति। / वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.30 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot remain still, for my mind is in tumult.
sanskrit: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते। / न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.31 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The omens are unfavorable; what good can come from the slaughter of my people on this battlefield?
sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव। / न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.32 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Ah, my Lord! I do not crave victory, nor a kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?
sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च। / किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.33 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: When those for whose sake I desire these things stand here, about to sacrifice their property and lives:
sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च। / त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.34 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Teachers, fathers, grandfathers, sons, grandsons, uncles, fathers-in-law, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.
sanskrit: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः। / मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.35 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: I would not kill them, even for three worlds; why then for this earth alone? It matters not if I myself am killed.
sanskrit: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन। / अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.36 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: My Lord! What happiness can come from the death of these sons of Dhritarashtra? We shall be committing a sin if we kill these desperate men.
sanskrit: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन। / पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.37 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: We are worthy of a nobler feat than slaughtering our relatives—the sons of Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be happy if we kill our kinsmen?
sanskrit: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्। / स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.38 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Although these men, blinded by greed, see no guilt in destroying their kin or fighting against their friends,
sanskrit: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः। / कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.39 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Should we not, whose eyes are open and who consider it wrong to annihilate our family, turn away from such a great crime?
sanskrit: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्। / कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.40 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The destruction of our kindred means the destruction of the traditions of our ancient lineage, and when these are lost, irreligion will overrun our homes.
sanskrit: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः। / धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.41 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: When irreligion spreads, the women of the house start to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the lineage follows.
sanskrit: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः। / स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.42 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, due to the lack of funeral cakes and ablutions.
sanskrit: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च। / पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.43 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: By the destruction of our lineage and the pollution of our blood, ancient class traditions and family purity alike perish.
sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः। / उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.44 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The wise say, my Lord, that they are forever lost whose ancient traditions have been lost.
sanskrit: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन। / नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.45 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Alas, it is strange that we should be willing to kill our own countrymen and commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the pleasures of kingdom.
sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्। / यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.46 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: If, on the contrary, the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, should slay me, unarmed and unresisting, surely that would be better for my welfare!
sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः। / धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 1.47 (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank into the seat of his chariot, discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed with grief in the midst of the armies."
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। / विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.1 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Sanjaya then told how the Lord Shri Krishna, seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with compassion, his eyes dimmed with flowing tears and full of despondency, consoled him:
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / तं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम्। / विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.2 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The Lord said: My beloved friend! Why yield to this weakness, on the eve of battle, which does no credit to those who call themselves Aryans and only brings them infamy, barring them from the gates of heaven?
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्। / अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.3 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O thou, who art the terror of thy enemies! Shake off such shameful effeminacy and make ready to act!
sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते। / क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.4 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Arjuna argued: My Lord! How can I, when the battle rages, send an arrow through Bheeshma and Drona, whom I should revere?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन। / इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.5 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Rather, I would be content with a beggar's crust than to kill these teachers of mine, these precious noble souls! To slay these masters who are my benefactors would be to stain the sweetness of life's pleasures with their blood.
sanskrit: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् / श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके। / हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव / भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.6 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Nor can I say whether it would be better for them to conquer me or for me to conquer them, since I would no longer care to live if I killed these sons of Dhritarashtra, who are now preparing for battle.
sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो / यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः। / यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम / स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.7 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.
sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः / पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः। / यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मे / शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.8 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: For even if I were to attain the monarchy of the visible world, or the sovereignty over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish that is now paralyzing my senses.
sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्या / द्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्। / अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम् / राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.9 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would not fight, and became silent, O King!
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप। / न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.10 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Thereupon, the Lord, with a gracious smile, addressed him who was so much depressed in the midst of the two armies.
sanskrit: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत। / सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.11 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, yet professing wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे। / गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.12 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.
sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः। / न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.13 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: As the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age in this body, so finally it passes into another; the wise have no delusion about this.
sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा। / तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.14 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Those external relations that bring cold and heat, pain and happiness come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!
sanskrit: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः। / आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.15 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstances, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, is only fit for immortality.
sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ। / समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.16 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: That which is not shall never be; that which is shall never cease to be. These truths are self-evident to the wise.
sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः। / उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.17 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The Spirit, which pervades all that is seen, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy it.
sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्। / विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.18 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The material bodies that this Eternal, Indestructible, and Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite; therefore, fight, O valiant man!
sanskrit: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः। / अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.19 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He who thinks that the Spirit kills, and he who thinks of it as killed, are both ignorant. The Spirit neither kills nor is it killed.
sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्। / उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.20 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: It was not born; it will never die, nor, once having been, can it cease to exist. Unborn, eternal, ever-enduring, yet most ancient, the spirit does not die when the body is dead.
sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि / न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। / अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो / न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.21 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He who knows the Spirit to be indestructible, immortal, unborn, and always the same, how should he kill or cause to be killed?
sanskrit: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्। / कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.22 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.
sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय / नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि। / तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा / न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.23 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Weapons cannot cleave it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot drench it, and wind cannot dry it.
sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः। / न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.24 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: It is impenetrable; it cannot be drowned, scorched, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervasive, unchanging, immovable, and most ancient.
sanskrit: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च। / नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.25 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable. Therefore, knowing the Spirit as such, you have no cause to grieve.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते। / तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.26 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Even if thou thinkest of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, O Mighty Man, thou still hast no cause to grieve.
sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्। / तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.27 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: For death is certain for that which is born, just as birth is certain for that which is dead. Therefore, do not grieve for what is inevitable.
sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च। / तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.28 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The end and beginning of beings are unknown; we only see the intervening formations. So, what is there to grieve about?
sanskrit: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत। / अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.29 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: One hears of the Spirit with surprise, another thinks it marvelous, the third listens without comprehending. Thus, though many are told about it, scarcely is there one who knows it.
sanskrit: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन / माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः। / आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति / श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.30 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Do not be anxious about these armies; the spirit in man is imperishable.
sanskrit: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत। / तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.31 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: You must look at your duty. Nothing can be more welcome to a soldier than a righteous war. Therefore, wavering in this resolve is unworthy, O Arjuna!
sanskrit: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि। / धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.32 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Blessed are the soldiers who find their opportunity; this opportunity has opened for thee the gates of heaven.
sanskrit: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्। / सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.33 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Refuse to fight in this righteous cause, and you will be a traitor, losing fame, incurring only sin.
sanskrit: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि। / ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.34 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Men will talk forever of thy disgrace; and to the noble, dishonor is worse than death.
sanskrit: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्। / संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.35 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Great generals will think that you have fled from the battlefield out of cowardice; though once honored, you will seem despicable.
sanskrit: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः। / येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.36 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Your enemies will spread scandal and mock your courage. Is there anything more humiliating?
sanskrit: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः। / निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.37 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: If you are killed, you will attain Heaven; if you are victorious, you will enjoy the kingdom of earth. Therefore, arise, O Son of Kunti, and fight!
sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्। / तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.38 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye. Be prepared for the combat, and you will commit no sin.
sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ। / ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.39 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: I have told you the philosophy of knowledge. Now, listen, and I will explain the philosophy of action, by means of which, O Arjuna, you will break through the bondage of all action.
sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु। / बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.40 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: On this path, endeavour is never wasted nor repressed. Even a little practice of it protects one from great danger.
sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते। / स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.41 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: By its means, the straying intellect becomes steadied in contemplating one object only; whereas the minds of the irresolute stray into innumerable bypaths.
sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन। / बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.42 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Only the ignorant speak in figurative language; it is they who extol the letter of the scriptures, saying, "There is nothing deeper than this."
sanskrit: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः। / वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.43 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Consulting only their own desires, they construct their own heaven, devising arduous and complex rites to secure their own pleasure and power; and the only result is rebirth.
sanskrit: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्। / क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.44 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: While their minds are absorbed with thoughts of power and personal enjoyment, they cannot focus their discrimination on one point.
sanskrit: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्। / व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.45 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The Vedic Scriptures tell of the three constituents of life—the Qualities. Rise above all of them, O Arjuna, above all the pairs of opposing sensations; be steadfast in truth, free from worldly anxieties, and centered in the Self.
sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन। / निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.46 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can extract from any scripture that which will serve their purpose.
sanskrit: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके। / तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.47 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: But you have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.
sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। / मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.48 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Revised: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.
sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय। / सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.49 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine. Therefore, have recourse to Pure Intelligence. It is only the small-minded who work for reward.
sanskrit: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय। / बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.50 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: When a person attains Pure Reason, they renounce in this world the results of both good and evil. Cling to Right Action. Spirituality is the true art of living.
sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते। / तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.51 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The sages, guided by pure intellect, renounce the fruits of their actions; and, thus freed from the shackles of rebirth, they attain the highest bliss.
sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः। / जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.52 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: When your reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then you will become indifferent to both the philosophies you have heard and those you may yet hear.
sanskrit: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति। / तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.53 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scriptures, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the infinite, then you have attained spirituality.
sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला। / समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.54 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognize the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? How does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव। / स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.55 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: When a person has given up the desires of their heart and is content with the Self alone, they have surely reached the highest state.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्। / आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.56 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The sage whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not aroused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger, or fear—take him to be one who stands at a lofty level.
sanskrit: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः। / वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.57 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He who, wherever he goes, is not attached to any person or place by ties of flesh; who accepts good and evil alike, neither welcoming the one nor shrinking from the other—take him to be one who is merged in the Infinite.
sanskrit: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्। / नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.58 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within its shell—take it that such a one has attained perfection.
sanskrit: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। / इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.59 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The objects of sense turn away from him who is abstinent. Even the taste for them is lost in him who has seen the Truth.
sanskrit: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः। / रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.60 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: O Arjuna! The mind of one who is attempting to conquer it is forcibly carried away, in spite of their efforts, by their tumultuous senses.
sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः। / इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.61 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Restraining them all, let him steadfastly meditate on Me; for whoever conquers their senses achieves perfection.
sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः। / वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.62 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: When a person dwells on the objects of sense, they create an attraction for them; this attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.
sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते। / सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.63 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Anger induces delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory results in the shattering of reason; and the destruction of reason leads to destruction.
sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः। / स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.64 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: But the self-controlled soul, who moves among sense objects, free from attachment or repulsion, wins eternal peace.
sanskrit: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्। / आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.65 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Having attained peace, he becomes free from misery; for when the mind gains peace, right discrimination follows.
sanskrit: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते। / प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.66 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Right discrimination is not for him who cannot concentrate. Without concentration, there cannot be meditation; he who cannot meditate must not expect peace; and without peace, how can one expect happiness?
sanskrit: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना। / न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.67 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते। / तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.68 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: Therefore, O Mighty-Armed One, he whose senses are detached from their objects—take it that his reason is purified.
sanskrit: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः। / इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.69 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The saint is awake when the world sleeps, and he disregards that for which the world lives.
sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी। / यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.70 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He attains peace into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which, though brimming with water, remains ever the same; not he whom desires carry away.
sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं / समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्। / तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे / स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.71 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: He attains peace who, giving up desire, moves through the world without aspiration, possessing nothing that he can call his own and is free from pride.
sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः। / निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 2.72 (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: O Arjuna! This is the state of the Self, the Supreme Spirit, to which, if one attains, it shall never be taken away. Even at the time of leaving the body, one will remain firmly enthroned there and become one with the Eternal.
sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति। / स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.1 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Arjuna questioned: My Lord! If wisdom is superior to action, why do you advise me to engage in this terrible fight?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन। / तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.2 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Your language confuses me and confounds my reason. Therefore, please tell me the only way by which I can, without doubt, secure my spiritual welfare.
sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे। / तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.3 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: In this world, as I have said, there is a twofold path, O sinless one! There is the path of wisdom for those who meditate, and the path of action for those who work.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ। / ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.4 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: No one can attain freedom from action by abstaining from action, nor can they reach perfection by simply not acting.
sanskrit: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते। / न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.5 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: He cannot remain inactive even for a moment, for the qualities of Nature will compel him to act, whether he wills it or not.
sanskrit: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्। / कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.6 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: He who remains motionless, refusing to act, yet brooding over sensuous objects, is that deluded soul simply a hypocrite.
sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्। / इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.7 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: But, O Arjuna! All honor to him whose mind controls his senses, for he is thereby beginning to practice Karma-Yoga, the Path of Right Action, keeping himself always unattached.
sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन। / कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.8 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Do your duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if one remained inactive.
sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः। / शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.9 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: In this world, people are fettered by their actions, unless they are performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let your actions be done without attachment, as a sacrifice only.
sanskrit: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः। / तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.10 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: In the beginning, when God created all beings through the sacrifice of Himself, He said to them: "You can procreate through sacrifice, and it shall satisfy all your desires."
sanskrit: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः। / अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.11 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Worship the powers of Nature, and let them nourish you in return; thus, supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.
sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः। / परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.12 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: For, fed by sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a thief.
sanskrit: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः। / तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.13 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: The sages who enjoy the food that remains after the sacrifice is made are freed from all sins; whereas, the selfish who spread their feast only for themselves feed on sin alone.
sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः। / भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.14 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: All creatures are the product of food; food is the product of rain; rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is the noblest form of action.
sanskrit: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः। / यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.15 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: All actions originate from the Supreme Spirit, which is Imperishable, and in sacrificial actions, the all-pervasive Spirit is consciously present.
sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्। / तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.16 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Thus, he who does not help the revolving wheel of sacrifice, but instead leads a sinful life, rejoicing in the gratification of his senses, O Arjuna, is breathing in vain.
sanskrit: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः। / अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.17 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: On the other hand, the soul who meditates on the Self is content to serve the Self and rests satisfied in the Self; there is nothing more for them to accomplish.
sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः। / आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.18 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: He has nothing to gain from the performance or non-performance of action; his welfare does not depend on any contribution that an earthly creature can make.
sanskrit: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन। / न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.19 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Therefore, do your duty perfectly, without worrying about the results, for he who does his duty without attachment attains the Supreme.
sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर। / असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.20 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of enlightening the world, it is your duty to act.
sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः। / लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.21 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: For whatever a great man does, others imitate; people conform to the standard he has set.
sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः। / स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.22 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: There is nothing in this universe, O Arjuna, that I am compelled to do, nor anything for me to attain; yet I persistently remain active.
sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन। / नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.23 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Were I not to act without ceasing, O prince, people would be inclined to do the same.
sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः। / मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.24 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: And if I were to refrain from action, the human race would be ruined; I would lead the world to chaos, and destruction would follow.
sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्। / सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.25 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: As the ignorant act, out of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.
sanskrit: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत। / कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.26 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: But a wise man should not disturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all others to do the same.
sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्। / जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.27 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Action is the product of the qualities inherent in nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says, "I am the doer."
sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः। / अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.28 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: But he, O Mighty One, who correctly understands the relationship between the Qualities and action, is not attached to the act, for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.
sanskrit: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः। / गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.29 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Those who do not understand the qualities are interested in the act; however, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of those who do not.
sanskrit: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु। / तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.30 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Therefore, surrender your actions to Me, keep your thoughts focused on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without expecting a reward, with a mind free from excitement, begin to fight.
sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा। / निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.31 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firmly in faith and without caviling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.
sanskrit: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः। / श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.32 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: But they who ridicule My word and do not observe it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom, and blind. They seek only their own destruction.
sanskrit: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्। / सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.33 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Even the wise man acts in accordance with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?
sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि। / प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.34 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: The love and hate that are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them, as they only obstruct the path.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ। / तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.35 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: It is better to do one's own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for doing the duty of another is fraught with danger.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। / स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.36 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is it that drives a person to sin, even against their will and as if by compulsion?"
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः। / अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.37 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts all things. It is the greatest enemy of man.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः। / महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.38 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: As fire is shrouded by smoke, a mirror is covered by dust, and a child is enveloped by the womb, so is the universe enveloped in desire.
sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च। / यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.39 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: It is the wise man's constant enemy; it tarnishes the face of wisdom, being as insatiable as a flame of fire.
sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा। / कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.40 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: It works through the senses, the mind, and the reason; and with their help, it destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते। / एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.41 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Therefore, O Arjuna, first control your senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin and is the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.
sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ। / पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.42 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: It is said that the senses are powerful; however, beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and greater than the intellect is He.
sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः। / मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 3.43 (Path of Selfless Service)
text: Thus, O Mighty-Armed One, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect, and with His help, subdue your personal ego and kill your enemy, Desire, even though it is extremely difficult.
sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना। / जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.1 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: I taught this imperishable philosophy to Vivaswān, the founder of the Sun dynasty; Vivaswān gave it to Manu, the lawgiver, and Manu to King Ikshvāku.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्। / विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.2 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: The Divine Kings knew it, for it was their tradition; then, after a long time, it was at last forgotten.
sanskrit: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः। / स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.3 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: It is the same ancient path that I have now revealed to you, for you are my devotee and my friend. It is the supreme secret.
sanskrit: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः। / भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.4 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Arjuna asked: My Lord! Vyasawana was born before You; how then can You have revealed it to him?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः। / कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.5 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to me, but yours are unknown to you.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन। / तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.6 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: There is no beginning to Me. Though I am imperishable and the Lord of all that exists, I manifest Myself by My own will and power.
sanskrit: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्। / प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.7 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Whenever spirituality decays and materialism is rampant, then, O Arjuna, I reincarnate myself.
sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। / अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.8 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked, and to establish the kingdom of God, I am reborn from age to age.
sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। / धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.9 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: He who realizes the divine truth concerning My birth and life does not take birth again; and when he leaves his body, he becomes one with Me.
sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः। / त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.10 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Many have merged their existences in Mine, being freed from desire, fear, and anger, always filled with Me and purified by the illuminating flame of self-abnegation.
sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः। / बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.11 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: However men try to worship Me, I welcome them. Whatever path they take, it leads to Me in the end.
sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्। / मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.12 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Those who seek success worship the Powers, and their actions in this world bear immediate fruit.
sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः। / क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.13 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: The four divisions of society—the wise, the soldier, the merchant, and the laborer—were created by Me, according to the natural distribution of qualities and instincts. I am the author of them, though I Myself do not act and am changeless.
sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः। / तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.14 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: My actions do not bind Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring. He who thus realizes Me is not enslaved by action.
sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा। / इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.15 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: In the light of wisdom, our ancestors who sought deliverance performed their acts. Act thou also as our fathers of old did.
sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः। / कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.16 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: What is action and what is inaction? This is a question that has bewildered the wise. But I will declare to you the philosophy of action, and knowing it, you will be free from evil.
sanskrit: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः। / तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.17 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: It is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, for the law of action is mysterious.
sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः। / अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.18 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: He who can see inaction in action, and action in inaction, is the wisest among men. He is a saint, even though he still acts.
sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः। / स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.19 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: The wise call him a sage, for whatever he undertakes is free from the motive of desire, and his deeds are purified by the fire of wisdom.
sanskrit: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः। / ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.20 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, he is always contented and independent; in reality, he does nothing, even though he appears to be acting.
sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः। / कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.21 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Expecting nothing, his mind and personality controlled, without greed, doing only bodily actions; though he acts, he remains untainted.
sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः। / शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.22 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Content with what comes to him without any effort of his own, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, his mind balanced in both success and failure; though he acts, the consequences do not bind him.
sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः। / समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.23 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: He who is without attachment, free, his mind centered in wisdom, and his actions done as a sacrifice, leave no trace behind.
sanskrit: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः। / यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.24 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: For him, the sacrifice is the Spirit; the Spirit and the offering are one; it is the Spirit that is sacrificed in its own fire, and the man, even in action, is united with God, since his mind never ceases to be fixed on Him while performing the act.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्। / ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.25 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Some sages sacrifice to the powers, while others offer themselves on the altar of the eternal.
sanskrit: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते। / ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.26 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Some sacrifice their physical senses in the fire of self-control; others offer up their contact with external objects in the sacrificial fire of their senses.
sanskrit: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति। / शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.27 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Others again sacrifice their activities and vitality in the spiritual fire of self-abnegation, kindled by wisdom.
sanskrit: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे। / आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.28 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Others offer as their sacrifice wealth, austerities, and meditation. Monks, wedded to their vows, renounce their scriptural learning and even their spiritual powers.
sanskrit: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे। / स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.29 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: There are some who practice controlling the vital energy and governing the subtle forces of prana and apana, thereby sacrificing their prana to apana, or their apana to prana.
sanskrit: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे। / प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.30 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Others, controlling their diet, sacrifice their worldly life to the spiritual fire. All understand the principle of sacrifice, and by it their sins are washed away.
sanskrit: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति। / सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.31 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Tasting the nectar of immortality, as the reward of sacrifice, they reach the Eternal. This world is not for those who refuse to sacrifice; nor is the other world.
sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्। / नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.32 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: In this way, other sacrifices may also be undertaken for the sake of the Spirit. Know that they all depend on action. Knowing this, you will be free.
sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे। / कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.33 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: The sacrifice of wisdom is superior to any material sacrifice, for, O Arjuna, the pinnacle of action is always realization.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप। / सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.34 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: This you shall learn by prostrating yourself at the master's feet, questioning them, and serving them. The wise who have realized the truth will teach you wisdom.
sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया। / उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.35 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Having known That, you shall never again be confounded; and, O Arjuna, by the power of that wisdom, you shall see all these people as if they were your own Self, and therefore as Me.
sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव। / येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.36 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Even if you are the greatest of sinners, you will cross over all sin by the ferryboat of wisdom.
sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः। / सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.37 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: As the kindled fire consumes the fuel, so, O Arjuna, the embers of action are burnt to ashes in the flame of wisdom.
sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन। / ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.38 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: There is nothing in the world so purifying as wisdom; and he who is a perfect saint finds that at last within himself.
sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते। / तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.39 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: He who is full of faith attains wisdom, and he who can control his senses, having attained that wisdom, will soon attain Supreme Peace.
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः। / ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.40 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: But the ignorant man, and he who has no faith, and the skeptic are lost. Neither in this world nor elsewhere is there any happiness in store for him who always doubts.
sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति। / नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.41 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: But the one who has renounced their actions for meditation, who has cleaved their doubts in two by the sword of wisdom, and who remains always enthroned in their Self, is not bound by their actions.
sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम्। / आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय

source: Bhagavad Gita 4.42 (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: Therefore, cleave asunder with the sword of wisdom the doubts of the heart, which your own ignorance has engendered, and follow the path of wisdom and arise!
sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः। / छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.1 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Arjuna said: My Lord! At one moment, You praise renunciation of action; at another, You praise right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is more conducive to my highest welfare?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि। / यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.2 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Both renunciation of action and the path of right action lead to the highest; however, right action is the better of the two.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ। / तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.3 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He is a true ascetic who never desires nor dislikes, who is unaffected by the opposites and is easily freed from bondage.
sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति। / निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.4 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Only the unenlightened speak of wisdom and right action as separate; the wise do not. If anyone knows one, they enjoy the fruit of both.
sanskrit: सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः। / एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.5 (Path of Renunciation)
text: The level which is attained through wisdom is also reached through right action. He who perceives that the two are one, knows the truth.
sanskrit: यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते। / एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.6 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Without concentration, O Mighty One, renunciation is difficult. But the sage who is always meditating on the Divine, shall soon attain the Absolute.
sanskrit: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः। / योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.7 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He who is spiritual, pure, has overcome his senses and his personal self, and has realized his highest Self as the Self of all—even though he acts, he is not bound by his actions.
sanskrit: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः। / सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.8 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Though the saint sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps, and breathes, yet he knows the truth and knows that it is not he who acts.
sanskrit: नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्। / पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.9 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Though he talks, gives, receives, opens his eyes, and shuts them, he still knows that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.
sanskrit: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि। / इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.10 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः। / लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.11 (Path of Renunciation)
text: The sage performs his action dispassionately, using his body, mind, intellect, and even his senses, always as a means for purification.
sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि। / योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.12 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Having abandoned the fruit of action, he wins eternal peace. Others, unacquainted with spirituality, led by desire and clinging to the benefit they think will follow their actions, become entangled in them.
sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्। / अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.13 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled soul enjoys bliss in this body, the city of the nine gates, neither doing anything themselves nor causing anything to be done.
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी। / नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.14 (Path of Renunciation)
text: The Lord of this universe has not ordained activity, nor any incentive thereto, nor any relation between an act and its consequences; all this is the work of Nature.
sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः। / न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.15 (Path of Renunciation)
text: The Lord does not accept responsibility for any person's sin or merit; they are deluded, for wisdom is submerged in ignorance within them.
sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः। / अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.16 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Surely, wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth to those whose ignorance has been dispelled by the wisdom of the Self.
sanskrit: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः। / तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.17 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Meditating on the divine, having faith in the divine, concentrating on the divine, and losing themselves in the divine, their sins dissolve in wisdom, and they go from whence there is no return.
sanskrit: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः। / गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.18 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Sages look upon all equally, whether they be a minister of learning and humility, an infidel, a cow, an elephant, or a dog.
sanskrit: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि। / शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.19 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Even in this world, those whose minds remain always balanced, fixed on the Supreme, conquer their earthly life; for the Supreme has neither blemish nor bias.
sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः। / निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.20 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He who knows and lives in the Absolute remains unmoved and unperturbed; he is not elated by pleasure nor depressed by pain.
sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्। / स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.21 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He finds happiness in his own Self and enjoys eternal bliss, whose heart does not yearn for the contacts of the earth and whose Self is one with the Everlasting.
sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्। / स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.22 (Path of Renunciation)
text: The joys that spring from external associations bring pain; they have their beginnings and their endings. The wise person does not rejoice in them.
sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते। / आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.23 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He who, before leaving his body, learns to overcome the promptings of desire and anger, is a saint and is happy.
sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्। / कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.24 (Path of Renunciation)
text: He who is happy within himself and has found its peace, and in whom the inner light shines, that sage attains eternal bliss and becomes one with the spirit.
sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः। / स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.25 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Sages whose sins have been washed away, whose sense of separateness has dissipated, who have subdued themselves, and seek only the welfare of all, come to the Eternal Spirit.
sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः। / छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.26 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Saints who know themselves, who control their minds, and feel neither desire nor anger, find eternal bliss everywhere.
sanskrit: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम्। / अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.27 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Excluding external objects, with his gaze fixed between the eyebrows, and the inward and outward breathings passing equally through his nostrils;
sanskrit: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः। / प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.28 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Governing sense, mind, and intellect, intent on liberation, free from desire, fear, and anger, the sage is eternally free.
sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः। / विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 5.29 (Path of Renunciation)
text: Knowing Me as the One who gladly receives all offerings of austerity and sacrifice, as the Mighty Ruler of all the Worlds and the Friend of all beings, he passes to Eternal Peace.
sanskrit: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्। / सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.1 (Path of Meditation)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts out of duty, without considering the consequences, is truly spiritual and a true ascetic; not he who merely observes rituals or shuns all action.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः। / स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.2 (Path of Meditation)
text: O Arjuna, renunciation is indeed what is known as right action. No one can become spiritually enlightened who has not renounced all desires.
sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव। / न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.3 (Path of Meditation)
text: For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when they have attained it, they must maintain themselves there through continual self-control.
sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते। / योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.4 (Path of Meditation)
text: When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, and is not interested in sense objects or any results that may flow from his acts, then he truly understands spirituality.
sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते। / सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.5 (Path of Meditation)
text: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.
sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। / आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.6 (Path of Meditation)
text: To one who has conquered their lower nature with its help, the Self is a friend; but to one who has not done so, it is an enemy.
sanskrit: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः। / अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.7 (Path of Meditation)
text: The Self of one who is self-controlled and has attained peace is equally unmoved by heat or cold, pleasure or pain, honor or dishonor.
sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः। / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.8 (Path of Meditation)
text: He who desires nothing but wisdom and spiritual insight, who has conquered his senses, and who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone, and fine gold with the same eye, is a real saint.
sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः। / युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.9 (Path of Meditation)
text: He looks impartially on all—lovers, friends, or foes; indifferent, hostile, alien, or relative; virtuous or sinful.
sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु। / साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.10 (Path of Meditation)
text: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with his mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.
sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः। / एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.11 (Path of Meditation)
text: Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat that is neither too high nor too low, and cover it with a grass mat, a deer skin, and a cloth.
sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः। / नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.12 (Path of Meditation)
text: Seated thus, with his mind concentrated, his functions controlled, and his senses governed, let him practice meditation for the purification of his lower nature.
sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः। / उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.13 (Path of Meditation)
text: Let him hold his body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.
sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः। / संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.14 (Path of Meditation)
text: With peace in his heart and no fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with his mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.
sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः। / मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.15 (Path of Meditation)
text: Thus, keeping his mind always in communion with Me and subduing his thoughts, he shall attain that Peace which is Mine and will lead him to liberation at last.
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः। / शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.16 (Path of Meditation)
text: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, nor for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overly addicted to sleep, nor for him who is always awake.
sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः। / न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.17 (Path of Meditation)
text: But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep, and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.
sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु। / युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.18 (Path of Meditation)
text: When the mind is completely controlled, centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then the man is truly spiritual.
sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते। / निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.19 (Path of Meditation)
text: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.
sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता। / योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.20 (Path of Meditation)
text: There, where the whole of nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the person abides within their Self and is satisfied there, their functions restrained by their union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.
sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया। / यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.21 (Path of Meditation)
text: When he enjoys the bliss that surpasses the senses and can only be grasped by the pure intellect, when he comes to rest within his highest self, he will never again stray from reality.
sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्। / वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.22 (Path of Meditation)
text: Finding That, he will realize that there is no possession so precious. And once established there, no calamity can disturb him.
sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः। / यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.23 (Path of Meditation)
text: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practiced with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed.
sanskrit: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्। / स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.24 (Path of Meditation)
text: Renouncing every desire that can be imagined, controlling the senses at every point through the power of the mind;
sanskrit: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः। / मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.25 (Path of Meditation)
text: Little by little, with the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.
sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया। / आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.26 (Path of Meditation)
text: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.
sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्। / ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.27 (Path of Meditation)
text: Supreme bliss is the lot of the sage whose mind attains peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.
sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम्। / उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.28 (Path of Meditation)
text: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys, without effort, the bliss that flows from the realization of the Infinite.
sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः। / सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.29 (Path of Meditation)
text: He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks upon everything with an impartial eye.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि। / ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.30 (Path of Meditation)
text: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.
sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति। / तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.31 (Path of Meditation)
text: The sage who realizes the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, no matter what their lot may be.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः। / सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.32 (Path of Meditation)
