text: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.
sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन। / सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.33 (Path of Meditation)
text: Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which You have revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन। / एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.34 (Path of Meditation)
text: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.
sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्। / तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.35 (Path of Meditation)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं। / अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.36 (Path of Meditation)
text: It is not possible to attain Self-Realization unless one knows how to control oneself; however, for one who, striving by the proper means, learns such control, it is possible.
sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः। / वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.37 (Path of Meditation)
text: Arjuna asked: What of him who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, yet retains his faith and does not attain perfection?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः। / अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.38 (Path of Meditation)
text: Having failed in both, my Lord, is he without hope, like a riven cloud with no support, lost on the spiritual path?
sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति। / अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.39 (Path of Meditation)
text: My Lord! You are worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; there is no one else competent to do so, save Yourself.
sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः। / त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.40 (Path of Meditation)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते। / नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.41 (Path of Meditation)
text: Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has strayed from the path of spirituality will be born again into the family of the pure, benevolent, and prosperous.
sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः। / शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.42 (Path of Meditation)
text: Or, he may be born in the family of wise sages, though such a birth is indeed very difficult to obtain.
sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्। / एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.43 (Path of Meditation)
text: Then, the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with it, he will more eagerly strive for perfection than before.
sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्। / यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.44 (Path of Meditation)
text: Unconsciously, he will return to the practices of his old life; thus, one who strives to attain spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who merely talks about it.
sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः। / जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.45 (Path of Meditation)
text: Then, after many lives of earnest striving and absolution of sins, the student of spirituality attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.
sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः। / अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.46 (Path of Meditation)
text: The wise person is superior to the ascetic, the scholar, and the man of action; therefore, be thou a wise person, O Arjuna!
sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः। / कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 6.47 (Path of Meditation)
text: I look upon him as the best of mystics, who, full of faith, worships Me and abides in Me.
sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना। / श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.1 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: Listen, O Arjuna! I will tell you how you can know Me in my full perfection. Practice meditation with your mind devoted to Me and take Me as your refuge.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः। / असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.2 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: I will reveal this knowledge to you and how it can be realized; once accomplished, there is nothing else worth having in this life.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः। / यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.3 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection, and even among those who gain occult powers, perhaps only one knows me in truth.
sanskrit: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये। / यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.4 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and personality—this is the eightfold division of My manifested nature.
sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च। / अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.5 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: This is My inferior nature; however, O valiant one, know that distinct from this is My superior nature, which is the very life that sustains the universe.
sanskrit: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम्। / जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.6 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: It is the womb of all beings; for I am He by Whom the worlds were created and shall be dissolved.
sanskrit: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय। / अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.7 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: O Arjuna! There is nothing higher than Me; all is strung on Me like rows of pearls on a thread.
sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय। / मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.8 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: O Arjuna! I am the fluidity in water, the light in the sun and moon, the mystic syllable Om in the Vedic scriptures, the sound in ether, and the virility in man.
sanskrit: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः। / प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.9 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: I am the fragrance of the earth, the brilliance of fire, the life force in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics.
sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ। / जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.10 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Know, O Arjuna, that I am the eternal seed of being; I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendour of the resplendent.
sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्। / बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.11 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: I am the strength of the strong, those who are free from attachment and desire; and, O Arjuna, I am the desire for righteousness.
sanskrit: बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम्। / धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.12 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Whatever be the nature of their life, whether it be pure, passionate, or ignorant, they are all derived from Me. They are in Me, but I am not in them.
sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये। / मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.13 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: The inhabitants of the world, misled by the natures engendered by the Qualities, do not know that I am higher than them all and that I do not change.
sanskrit: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत्। / मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.14 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Verily, this divine illusion of phenomenon manifesting itself in the qualities is difficult to surmount. Only they who devote themselves exclusively to Me can accomplish it.
sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया। / मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.15 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: The sinner, the ignorant, the vile, deprived of spiritual perception by the glamour of illusion, and he who leads a godless life—none of them shall find me.
sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः। / माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.16 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: O Arjuna! The righteous who worship Me are grouped in stages: first, those who suffer, next those who desire knowledge, then those who thirst after truth, and lastly those who attain wisdom.
sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन। / आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.17 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Of all these, he who has gained wisdom, who meditates on Me without ceasing, devoting himself solely to Me, is the best; for I am exceedingly beloved by the wise man, and the wise man is also beloved by Me.
sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते। / प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.18 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Noble-minded are they all, but the wise man I hold as my own self; for he, remaining always at peace with me, makes me his ultimate goal.
sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्। / आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.19 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: After many lives, at last the wise one realizes Me as I am. It is very difficult to find a man so enlightened that he sees God everywhere.
sanskrit: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते। / वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.20 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: They in whom wisdom is obscured by one desire or another, worship the lesser powers, practicing many rites that vary according to their temperaments.
sanskrit: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः। / तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.21 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: But whatever form of worship, if the devotee has faith, then I set My own seal upon their faith in that worship.
sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति। / तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.22 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: If he worships one form alone with real faith, then his desires shall be fulfilled through that alone; for thus I have ordained.
sanskrit: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते। / लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.23 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: The fruit that comes to people of limited insight is, after all, finite. Those who worship the Lower Powers attain them; but those who worship Me come to Me alone.
sanskrit: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम्। / देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.24 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: The ignorant think of Me, who am the Unmanifested Spirit, as if I were in human form. They do not understand that My Superior Nature is unchanging and most excellent.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः। / परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.25 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: I am not visible to all, for I am enveloped by the illusion of the Phenomenon. This deluded world does not know Me as the Unborn and Imperishable.
sanskrit: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः। / मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.26 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: I know, O Arjuna, all beings in the past, the present, and the future; but they do not know Me.
sanskrit: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन। / भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.27 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: O brave Arjuna! Man lives in a fantastical world, deceived by the glamour of opposing sensations, infatuated by desire and aversion.
sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत। / सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.28 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: But those who act righteously, in whom sin has been destroyed, who are free from the infatuation of conflicting emotions, they worship Me with a firm resolve.
sanskrit: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्। / ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.29 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Those who make Me their refuge, striving for liberation from decay and death, realize the Supreme Spirit, which is their own real Self, and in which all action finds its consummation.
sanskrit: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये। / ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 7.30 (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: Those who see Me in the life of the world, in the universal sacrifice, and as pure Divinity, keeping their minds steady, they live in Me even in the hour of death's approach.
sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः। / प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.1 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Arjuna asked: O Lord of Lords! What is that which people call the Supreme Spirit, what is humanity's spiritual nature, and what is the law? What is matter and what is divinity?
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम। / अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.2 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Who rules the spirit sacrifice in many, and how may those who have learned self-control come to the knowledge of Thee at the time of death?
sanskrit: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन। / प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.3 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The Lord Shri Krishna replied: The Supreme Spirit is the Highest Imperishable Self, and Its nature is spiritual consciousness. The worlds have been created and are sustained by an emanation from the Spirit, which is called the Law.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते। / भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.4 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Matter consists of forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of their race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.
sanskrit: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्। / अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.5 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Whosoever, at the time of death, thinks only of Me and, thinking thus, leaves the body and goes forth, will assuredly know Me.
sanskrit: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्। / यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.6 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Whatever sphere of being the mind of a man is intent on at the time of death, to that he will go.
sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्। / तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.7 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Therefore, always meditate on Me and fight; if your mind and reason are fixed on Me, you will surely come to Me.
sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च। / मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.8 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: He whose mind does not wander, and who is engaged in constant meditation, attains the Supreme Spirit.
sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना। / परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.9 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Whoso meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, more minute than an atom, yet the Ruler and Upholder of all, Unimaginable, Brilliant like the Sun, Beyond the reach of darkness;
sanskrit: कविं पुराणमनुशासितार / मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः। / सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप / मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.10 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: He who leaves the body with an unmoved mind, filled with devotion, and by the power of his meditation gathers his whole vital energy between his eyebrows, attains the Supreme.
sanskrit: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन / भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव। / भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् / स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.11 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Now, I will briefly speak of the imperishable goal, proclaimed by those who are versed in the scriptures, which the mystic attains when free from passion, and for which they are content to undergo the vow of continence.
sanskrit: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति / विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः। / यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति / तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.12 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Closing the gates of the body, drawing the forces of his mind into the heart, and, by the power of meditation, concentrating his vital energy in the brain;
sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च। / मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.13 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Repeating Om, the symbol of eternity, and holding Me always in remembrance, he who thus leaves his body and goes forth reaches the Supreme Spirit.
sanskrit: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन्। / यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.14 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: To him who constantly thinks of Me and nothing else, to such an ever-faithful devotee, O Arjuna, I am ever accessible.
sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः। / तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.15 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Coming to Me in this way, these great souls no longer go to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have achieved perfection.
sanskrit: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्। / नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.16 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The worlds, along with the entire realm of creation, come and go; but, O Arjuna, whoever comes to Me, for them there is no rebirth.
sanskrit: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन। / मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.17 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Those who understand the cosmic day and night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.
sanskrit: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः। / रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.18 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: At the dawn of that day, all objects in manifestation stream forth from the Unmanifest, and when evening falls, they are dissolved back into it again.
sanskrit: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे। / रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.19 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus, it is ordained.
sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते। / रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.20 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: In truth, therefore, there is the eternal, unmanifest, which is beyond and above the unmanifest spirit of creation, and which is never destroyed when all these beings perish.
sanskrit: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः। / यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.21 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The wise say that the Unmanifest and Indestructible is the highest goal of all; when once that is reached, there is no returning. That is my blessed home.
sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम्। / यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.22 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: O Arjuna! That Highest God, in Whom all beings abide, and Who pervades the entire universe, is reached only by wholehearted devotion. *He is the one who determines the course of worldly events and the destiny of all living beings.*
sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया। / यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.23 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: Now, I will tell you, O Arjuna, the times at which, if the mystics go forth, they do not return, and at which they go forth only to return.
sanskrit: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः। / प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.24 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: If the sage, knowing the Supreme Spirit, goes forth with fire and light during the day, in the fortnight of the waxing moon, and in the six months before the Northern summer solstice, he will attain the Supreme.
sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम्। / तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.25 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: But if he departs in gloom, at night, during the fortnight of the waning moon and in the six months before the winter solstice, then he reaches only lunar light and he will be reborn.
sanskrit: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्। / तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.26 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: These bright and dark paths out of the world have always existed. Whoever takes the former, does not return; he who chooses the latter, returns.
sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते। / एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.27 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: O Arjuna! The saint, knowing these paths, is not confused; therefore, meditate perpetually.
sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन। / तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 8.28 (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The sage who knows this passes beyond all merit that comes from the study of the scriptures, from sacrifice, from austerities, and from charity, and reaches the Supreme Primeval Abode.
sanskrit: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव / दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम्। / अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा / योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.1 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: I will now reveal to you, since you do not doubt, that profound mysticism, which, when followed with experience, will liberate you from sin.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे। / ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.2 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: This is the supreme science, the supreme secret, the purest and best; it is intuitive, righteous, and to those who practice it, it is exceedingly pleasant.
sanskrit: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्। / प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.3 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: They who have no faith in this teaching cannot find Me; they remain lost in the purlieus of this perishable world.
sanskrit: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप। / अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.4 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: The whole world is pervaded by Me, yet My form is not visible. All living beings have their being in Me, yet I am not confined by them.
sanskrit: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना। / मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.5 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Nevertheless, they do not consciously abide in Me. Such is My Divine Sovereignty that, though I, the Supreme Self, am the cause and upholder of all, yet I remain outside.
sanskrit: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्। / भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.6 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: As the mighty wind, though moving everywhere, has no resting place except in space, so all these beings have no home except in Me.
sanskrit: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान्। / तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.7 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: All beings, O Arjuna, return at the end of every cosmic cycle into the realm of Nature, which is a part of Me, and at the start of the next I send them forth again.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम्। / कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.8 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: With the help of Nature, I again and again pour forth the whole multitude of beings, whether they will or not, for they are ruled by My will.
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः। / भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.9 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: But these acts of mine do not bind me; I remain outside and unattached.
sanskrit: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय। / उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.10 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Under my guidance, Nature produces all movable and immovable things. Thus, O Arjuna, this universe revolves.
sanskrit: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम्। / हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.11 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Fools disregard Me, seeing Me clad in human form. They do not know that in My higher nature, I am the Lord-God of all.
sanskrit: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम्। / परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.12 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Their hopes are futile, their actions worthless, their knowledge ineffective; they are without sense, deceitful, barbaric, and godless.
sanskrit: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः। / राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.13 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: But the great souls, O Arjuna! Filled with my divine spirit, they worship me, fix their minds on me alone, for they know that I am the imperishable source of being.
sanskrit: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः। / भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.14 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Always extolling Me, they are strenuous and firm in their vows, prostrating themselves before Me, and worshiping Me continually with concentrated devotion.
sanskrit: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः। / नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.15 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Others worship Me with full consciousness as the One, the Manifold, the Omnipresent, and the Universal.
sanskrit: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते। / एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.16 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the oblation, the sacrifice, and the worship; I am the fuel and the chant; I am the butter offered to the fire; I am the fire itself, and I am the act of offering.
sanskrit: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम्। / मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.17 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the Father of the universe, its Mother, Nourisher, and Grandfather; I am the Knowable and the Pure; I am Om, and I am the Sacred Scriptures.
sanskrit: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः। / वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.18 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the goal, the sustainer, the Lord, the witness, the home, the shelter, the lover, and the origin; I am life and death; I am the fountain and the imperishable seed.
sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत्। / प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.19 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the heat of the sun, I release and withhold the rain. I am death and immortality; I am being and non-being.
sanskrit: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च। / अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.20 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Those who are versed in the scriptures, who drink the mystic Soma-juice and are purified from sin, and who, while worshipping Me with sacrifices, pray that I will lead them to heaven; they reach the holy world where the Controller of the Powers of Nature resides, and they enjoy the feasts of Paradise.
sanskrit: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा / यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते। / ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक / मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.21 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Yet, although they enjoy the spacious glories of Paradise, when their merit is exhausted, they are born again into this world of mortals. They have followed the letter of the scriptures, yet, because they have sought to fulfill their own desires, they must depart and return again and again.
sanskrit: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं / क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति। / एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना / गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.22 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: But if a person meditates on Me and Me alone, worships Me always and everywhere, I will take upon Myself the fulfillment of their aspiration, and I will safeguard whatever they attain.
sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते। / तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.23 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Even those who worship the lesser powers, if they do so with faith, they are thereby worshipping Me, though not in the correct manner.
sanskrit: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः। / तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.24 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the willing recipient of sacrifice, and I am its true Lord. But they do not know me truly, so they fall back.
sanskrit: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च। / न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.25 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: The votaries of the lesser powers go to them; the devotees of spirits go to them; they who worship the powers of darkness, to such powers shall they go; and so too, those who worship me shall come to me.
sanskrit: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः। / भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.26 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Whatever a person offers to Me, be it a leaf, flower, fruit, or water, I accept it, for it is offered with devotion and a pure mind.
sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति। / तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.27 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you sacrifice and give, whatever austerities you practice, do all as an offering to Me.
sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत्। / यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.28 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: So, your action will have no result, either good or bad; but, through the spirit of renunciation, you will come to Me and be free.
sanskrit: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः। / संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.29 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: I am the same to all beings; I do not favour any, nor do I hate any. However, those who worship Me devotedly, they live in Me and I in them.
sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः। / ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.30 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Even the most sinful, if he worships Me with his whole heart, shall be considered righteous, for he is treading the right path.
sanskrit: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक्। / साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.31 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: He will soon attain spirituality and eternal peace. O Arjuna! Believe me, my devotee is never lost.
sanskrit: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति। / कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.32 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Even the children of sinful parents, those miscalled the weaker sex, merchants, and laborers, if they make Me their refuge, they shall attain the highest.
sanskrit: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः। / स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.33 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: What need is there, then, to mention the holy ministers of God, the devotees, and the saintly rulers? Therefore, do you, born in this changing and miserable world, also worship Me.
sanskrit: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा। / अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 9.34 (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: Fix your mind on Me, devote yourself to Me, sacrifice for Me, surrender to Me, make Me the object of your aspirations, and you shall assuredly become one with Me, Who am your own Self.
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु। / मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.1 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna said: Now, O Prince! Listen to My supreme advice, which I give you for the sake of your welfare, for you are My beloved.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / भूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः। / यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.2 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Neither the professors of divinity nor the great ascetics know My origin, for I am the source from which they all originate.
sanskrit: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः। / अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.3 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: He who knows Me as the unborn, without beginning, the Lord of the universe, he, stripped of his delusions, becomes free from all conceivable sins.
sanskrit: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम्। / असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.4 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Intelligence, wisdom, non-delusion, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calmness, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear, and fearlessness;
sanskrit: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः। / सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.5 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Harmlessness, equanimity, contentment, austerity, beneficence, fame, and failure—all these characteristics of beings spring from Me alone.
sanskrit: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः। / भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.6 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: The seven Great Seers, the progenitors of mankind, the Ancient Four, and the Lawgivers were born of My will and come forth directly from Me. The race of mankind has sprung from them. (Mareechi, Atri, Angira, Pulah, Kratu, Pulastya, Vahishta; the Masters: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan, Sanatkumar.)
sanskrit: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा। / मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.7 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: He who rightly understands My manifested glory and My creative power attains perfect peace without a doubt.
sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः। / सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.8 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the source of all; from me everything flows. Therefore, the wise worship me with an unchanging devotion.
sanskrit: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते। / इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.9 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: With minds concentrated on Me, with lives absorbed in Me, and enlightening one another, they ever feel content and happy.
sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम्। / कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.10 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: To those who are always devout and who worship Me with love, I give the power of discrimination that leads them to Me.
sanskrit: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम्। / ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.11 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: By My grace, I live in their hearts, and I dispel the darkness of ignorance with the shining light of wisdom.
sanskrit: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः। / नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.12 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Arjuna asked: Thou art the Supreme Spirit, the Eternal Home, the Holiest of Holies, the Eternal Divine Self, the Primal God, the Unborn, and Omnipresent.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान्। / पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.13 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: So have said the seers, the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa; and Thou Thyself also sayest it.
sanskrit: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा। / असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.14 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I believe in what You have said, my Lord! For neither the godly nor the godless comprehend Your manifestation.
sanskrit: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव। / न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.15 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: You alone know Yourself, by the power of Your Self; You are the Supreme Spirit, the Source and Master of all being, the Lord of Lords, the Ruler of the Universe.
sanskrit: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम। / भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.16 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Please tell me about all of Your glorious manifestations, through which You pervade the world.
sanskrit: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः। / याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.17 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: O Master! How can I, through constant meditation, come to know You? My Lord! What are Your various manifestations through which I can meditate on You?
sanskrit: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन्। / केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.18 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Tell me again, I pray, of Thy power and Thy glory in full; for I feel that I am never satisfied when I listen to Thy immortal words.
sanskrit: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन। / भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.19 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: So be it, My beloved friend! I will unfold to you some of the chief aspects of My glory. There is no end to its full extent.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः। / प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.20 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: O Arjuna! I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, the life, and the end of them all.
sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः। / अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.21 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of all the creative powers, I am the Creator; of luminaries, the Sun; of winds, the Whirlwind; and of planets, the Moon.
sanskrit: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान्। / मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.22 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of the Vedas, I am the hymns; I am the electric force in the powers of nature; of the senses, I am the mind; and I am the intelligence in all that lives.
sanskrit: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः। / इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.23 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Among forces of vitality, I am the life; I am Mammon to the heathens and the godless; I am the energy in fire, earth, wind, sky, heaven, sun, moon, and planets; and among mountains, I am Mount Meru.
sanskrit: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम्। / वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.24 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Among the priests, know, O Arjuna, that I am the priest Brihaspati; of generals, I am Skanda, the Commander-in-Chief, and of waters, I am the Ocean.
sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम्। / सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.25 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of the great seers, I am Bhrigu; of words, I am Om; of offerings, I am the silent prayer; among things immovable, I am the Himalayas.
sanskrit: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम्। / यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.26 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of trees, I am the sacred fig tree; of divine seers, Narada; of heavenly singers, I am Chitraratha, their leader; and of sages, I am Kapila.
sanskrit: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः। / गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.27 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Know that among horses I am Pegasus, heaven-born; among the lordly elephants I am the white one, and I am the ruler among men.
sanskrit: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम्। / ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.28 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the thunderbolt among weapons; I am the Cow of Plenty among cows; I am Passion in those who procreate, and I am the Cobra among serpents.
sanskrit: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक्। / प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.29 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the king-python among snakes, I am the aqueous principle among those that live in water, I am the father of fathers, and among rulers I am death.
sanskrit: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्। / पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.30 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: And I am the devotee Prahlada among the heathens; of Time I am the Eternal Present; I am the Lion among beasts and the Eagle among birds.
sanskrit: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्। / मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.31 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the wind among purifiers, the king Rama among warriors; I am the crocodile among fishes, and I am the Ganges among rivers.
sanskrit: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम्। / झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.32 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of creation; among sciences, I am the science of spirituality; I am the discussion among disputants.
sanskrit: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन। / अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.33 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of letters, I am A; I am the copulative in compound words; I am inexhaustible Time; and I am the all-pervading Preserver.
sanskrit: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च। / अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.34 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am all-devouring Death; I am the Origin of all that will happen; I am Fame, Fortune, Speech, Memory, Intellect, Constancy, and Forgiveness.
sanskrit: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम्। / कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.35 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Of hymns, I am Brihatsama; of meters, I am Garatri; among months, I am Margasheersha (December); and I am Spring among seasons.
sanskrit: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम्। / मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.36 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the gambler's cheat and the splendor of the splendid; I am victory; I am effort; and I am the purity of the pure.
sanskrit: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्। / जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.37 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am Shri Krishna among the Vishnu-clan, Arjuna among the Pandavas, Vyasa among the saints, and Shukracharya among the sages.
sanskrit: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः। / मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.38 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the scepter of rulers, the strategy of conquerors, the silence of mystery, and the wisdom of the wise.
sanskrit: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम्। / मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.39 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: I am the seed of all beings, O Arjuna! No creature, moving or unmoving, can live without Me.
sanskrit: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन। / न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.40 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: O Arjuna! The aspects of My divine life are endless; I have mentioned only a few as an example.
sanskrit: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप। / एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.41 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: Whatever is glorious, excellent, beautiful, and mighty, be assured that it comes from a fragment of My splendor.
sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा। / तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 10.42 (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: But what is the use of all these details to you, O Arjuna? I sustain this universe with only a small part of Myself.
sanskrit: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन। / विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.1 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Arjuna said: My Lord! Your words concerning the Supreme Secret of Self, given for my blessing, have dispelled the illusions that surrounded me.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम्। / यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.2 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: O Lord, whose eyes are like the lotus petal! You have described in detail the origin and dissolution of beings, and Your own Eternal Majesty.
sanskrit: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया। / त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.3 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: I believe all as you have declared it. I now long to have a vision of your divine form, O Most High!
sanskrit: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर। / द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.4 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: If you think it is possible for me to see it, show me, O Lord of Lords, your eternal self.
sanskrit: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो। / योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.5 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: "Behold, O Arjuna! My celestial forms, by the hundreds and thousands, various in kind, color, and shape."
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। / नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.6 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Behold, thou seest the powers of Nature: fire, earth, wind, and sky; the sun, the heavens, the moon, the stars; all forces of vitality and healing; and the roving winds. Behold, thou seest the myriad wonders revealed to none but thee.
sanskrit: पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा। / बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.7 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Here, living in Me, O Arjuna, behold the entire universe, both movable and immovable, and anything else you would like to see!
sanskrit: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम्। / मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.8 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Yet, since you cannot see Me with mortal eyes, behold, I give you divine sight. Now, see the glory of My sovereignty.
sanskrit: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा। / दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.9 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Sanjaya continued: "Having thus spoken, O King, the Lord Shri Krishna, the Almighty Prince of Wisdom, showed Arjuna the Supreme Form of the Great God.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः। / दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.10 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: There were countless eyes, mouths, and innumerable mystic forms, with shining ornaments and flaming celestial weapons.
sanskrit: अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम्। / अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.11 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Crowned with heavenly garlands, clothed in shining garments, anointed with divine unguents, He showed Himself as the Resplendent One, Marvelous, Boundless, and Omnipresent.
sanskrit: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम्। / सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.12 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Could a thousand suns blaze forth together, it would be but a faint reflection of the radiance of the Lord God.
sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता। / यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.13 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: In that vision, Arjuna saw the universe, with its manifold shapes, all embraced in one, its Supreme Lord.
sanskrit: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा। / अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.14 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Then, Arjuna, filled with awe, his hair standing on end, bowing his head, and clasping his hands in reverence, spoke to the Lord:
sanskrit: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः। / प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.15 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Arjuna said: O Almighty God! I see in You the powers of Nature, the various creatures of the world, the Progenitor on His lotus throne, the Sages, and the shining angels.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे / सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान्। / ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ / मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.16 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: I see You, infinite in form, with faces, eyes, and limbs everywhere; with no beginning, middle, or end. O You, Lord of the Universe, whose form is universal!
sanskrit: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं / पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्। / नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं / पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.17 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: I see you with the crown, the scepter, and the discus; a blaze of splendor. Scarcely can I gaze upon you, so radiant you are, glowing like a blazing fire, brilliant as the sun, immeasurable.
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च / तेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम्। / पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता / द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.18 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: You are imperishable, the only one worthy of being known, the priceless treasure-house of the universe, the immortal guardian of eternal life, and the everlasting spirit.
sanskrit: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं / त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्। / त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता / सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.19 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Without beginning, without middle, and without end, infinite in power, with arms all-embracing, the sun and moon as Your eyes, Your face beaming with the fire of sacrifice, flooding the whole universe with light.
sanskrit: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य / मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम्। / पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम् / स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.20 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Alone, you fill all the quarters of the sky, earth, and heaven, and the regions between. O Almighty Lord! Seeing your marvelous and awe-inspiring form, the spheres tremble with fear.
sanskrit: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि / व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः। / दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं / लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.21 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: The troops of celestial beings enter into You, some invoking You in fear, with folded palms; the great seers and adepts sing hymns to Your glory, saying, "All hail!"
sanskrit: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्ति / केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति। / स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः / स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.22 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: The vital forces, major stars, fire, earth, air, sky, sun, heaven, moon, and planets; the angels, guardians of the universe, divine healers, winds, fathers, heavenly singers, and hosts of mammon-worshippers, demons, and saints are all amazed.
sanskrit: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या / विश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च। / गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा / वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.23 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Seeing Thy stupendous Form, O Most Mighty One, with its myriad faces, its innumerable eyes, limbs, and terrible jaws, I myself and all the worlds are overwhelmed with awe.
sanskrit: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं / महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्। / बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं / दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.24 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: When I see You, touching the heavens, glowing with color, with open mouth and wide, fiery eyes, I am terrified. O my Lord! My courage and peace of mind abandon me.
sanskrit: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं / व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्। / दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा / धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.25 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: When I see Thy mouths with their fearful jaws, like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation, I lose all sense of place and find no rest. Be merciful, O Lord, in whom this universe abides!
sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि / दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि। / दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म / प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.26 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: All these sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of princes, Bheeshma, Drona, and Karna, as well as the other warrior chiefs on our side;
sanskrit: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः / सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः। / भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौ / सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.27 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: 1 See them all rushing headlong into Thy mouths, with terrible tusks, horrible to behold. Some are mangled between Thy jaws, with their heads crushed to atoms.
sanskrit: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति / दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि। / केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु / संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.28 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: As rivers in flood surge furiously towards the ocean, so these heroes, the greatest among men, fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths.
sanskrit: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः / समुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति। / तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा / विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.29 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: As moths impetuously fly towards the flame, only to be killed, so these men rush into Your mouths to court their own destruction.
sanskrit: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा / विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः। / तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका / स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.30 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: You seem to swallow up the worlds, lapping them in flame. Your glory fills the universe. Your fierce rays beat down upon it irresistibly.
sanskrit: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता / ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः। / तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं / भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.31 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Tell me then, who are You, who wears this dreadful form? I bow before You, O Mighty One! Have mercy, I pray, and let me see You as You were at first. I do not know what Your intentions are.
sanskrit: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो / नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद। / विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं / न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.32 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have shown myself to you as the Destroyer who lays waste the world and whose purpose is destruction. In spite of your efforts, all these warriors gathered for battle shall not escape death.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो / लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः। / ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे / येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.33 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Then gird up your loins and conquer. Subdue your foes and enjoy the kingdom in prosperity. I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!
sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व / जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्। / मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव / निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.34 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Drona, Bheeshma, Jayadratha, Karna, and other brave warriors - I have condemned them all. Destroy them; fight without fear. Your foes shall be crushed."
sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च / कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान्। / मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा / युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.35 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Sanjaya continued: "Having heard these words from the Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince Arjuna, with folded hands trembling, prostrated himself and with a choked voice, bowing down again and again, and overwhelmed with awe, once more addressed the Lord.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य / कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी। / नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं / सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.36 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Arjuna said: My Lord! It is natural for the world to revel and rejoice when singing praises of Your glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer You their salutations.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या / जगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च। / रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति / सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.37 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: How else should they do? O Supreme Self, greater than the powers of creation, the first cause, infinite, the Lord of Lords, the home of the universe, imperishable, being and non-being, yet transcending both.
sanskrit: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन् / गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे। / अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास / त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.38 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: You are the Primal God, the Ancient One, the Supreme Abode of this universe, the Knower, the Knowledge, and the Final Home. You fill everything. Your form is infinite.
sanskrit: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण / स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्। / वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम / त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.39 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: You are the wind, you are death, you are the fire, the water, the moon, the father, and the grandfather. Honor and glory to you a thousand and a thousand times! Again and again, salutations to you, O my Lord!
sanskrit: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः / प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च। / नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः / पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.40 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Salutations to Thee in front and on all sides, Thou who encompasseth me round about. Thy power is infinite; Thy majesty immeasurable; Thou upholdest all things; indeed, Thou Thyself art All.
sanskrit: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते / नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व। / अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं / सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.41 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Whatever I have said to you in rashness, taking you only as a friend and addressing you as “O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend!” in thoughtless familiarity, without understanding your greatness;
sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं / हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति। / अजानता महिमानं तवेदं / मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.42 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Whatever insults I have offered to You in jest, in sport, in repose, in conversation, or at a banquet, alone or in a crowd, I ask for Your forgiveness for them all, O You Who are without equal!
sanskrit: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि / विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु। / एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं / तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.43 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: For you are the Father of all things movable and immovable, the Worshipful, the Master of Masters! In all the worlds, there is none equal to you; how then could there be one superior, O you who stand alone, Supreme?
sanskrit: पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य / त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान्। / न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो / लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.44 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Therefore, I prostrate myself before You, O Lord! Most Adorable! I salute You, and I ask for Your blessing. Only You can be trusted to bear with me, like a father to a son, like a friend to a friend, and like a lover to his beloved.
sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं / प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम्। / पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः / प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.45 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: I rejoice that I have seen what no man has ever seen before; yet, O Lord! I am overwhelmed with fear. Please take on the form I know. Be merciful, O Lord! You who are the home of the entire universe.
sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा / भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे। / तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं / प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.46 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: I long to see Thee as Thou wert before, with the crown, the scepter, and the discus in Thy hands; in Thy other form, with Thy four hands, O Thou whose arms are countless and whose forms are infinite.
sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त / मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव। / तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन / सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.47 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved friend! It is only through My grace and power that you have been able to see this vision of splendour, the Universal, the Infinite, the Original. Never has it been seen by anyone else.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं / रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात्। / तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं / यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.48 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: It is not possible for man on earth to see what thou hast seen, O thou foremost hero of the Kuru-clan, through study of the scriptures, sacrifice or gift, ritual or rigorous austerity!
sanskrit: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै / र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः। / एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके / द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.49 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Do not be afraid or confused by the terrible vision. Put away your fear and, with a joyful mind, see Me again in My usual form.
sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो / दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम्। / व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं / तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.50 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Sanjaya continued: "Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Lord Shri Krishna showed Himself again in His accustomed form; and the Mighty Lord, in gentle tones, softly consoled him who had recently trembled with fear.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच / इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा / स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः। / आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं / भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.51 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Arjuna said: Seeing You in Your gentle human form, my Lord, I am myself again, calm once more.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन। / इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.52 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: It is difficult to see the vision of Me that thou hast seen. Even the most powerful have longed for it in vain.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम। / देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.53 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: It is not possible to see Me as you have done through studying the scriptures, performing austerities, giving gifts, or making sacrifices.
sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया। / शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.54 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: Only through tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only in this way can a person become one with Me, O Arjuna!
sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन। / ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप

source: Bhagavad Gita 11.55 (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: He who does every action for My sake, to whom I am the final goal, who loves Me alone and hates no one—O My dearest son, only he can realize Me!
sanskrit: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः। / निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.1 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, which are the better devotees who worship You: those who try to know You as a Personal God, or those who worship You as Impersonal and Indestructible?"
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.2 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Those who keep their minds fixed on Me, who worship Me always with unwavering faith and concentration, are the very best.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.3 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Those who worship Me as the Indestructible, the Undefinable, the Omnipresent, the Unthinkable, the Primal, the Immutable, and the Eternal;
sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते।सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.4 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Subduing their senses, viewing all conditions of life with an equal eye, and working for the welfare of all beings, they assuredly come to Me.
sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.5 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: But they who fix their attention on the Absolute and Impersonal encounter greater hardships, for it is difficult for those who have a body to realize Me as without one.
sanskrit: क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम्। / अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.6 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Verily, those who surrender their actions to Me, who contemplate Me, worship Me, and meditate on Me alone, with no thought other than Me.
sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः।अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.7 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: O Arjuna! I rescue them from the ocean of life and death, for their minds are fixed upon Me.
sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात्।भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.8 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Then let your mind cling only to Me, let your intellect abide in Me; and without doubt, you will live hereafter in Me alone.
sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.9 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: But if you cannot fix your mind firmly on Me, then, my beloved friend, try to do so through constant practice.
sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.10 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: And if you are not strong enough to practice concentration, then devote yourself to My service, do all your acts for My sake, and you will still attain the goal.
sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव।मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.11 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: And if thou art too weak to do even this, then seek refuge in union with Me, and with perfect self-control renounce the fruits of thy actions.
sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः।सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.12 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Knowledge is superior to blind action, meditation is superior to knowledge, renunciation of the fruit of action is superior to meditation, and peace follows from renunciation.
sanskrit: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते।ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.13 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: He who is incapable of hatred towards any being, who is kind and compassionate, free from selfishness, without pride, equable in pleasure and pain, and forgiving—
sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.14 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Always content, self-centered, self-controlled, resolute, with mind and reason dedicated to Me, such a devotee of Mine is beloved to Me.
sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः।मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.15 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: He who does not harm the world, and whom the world cannot harm, who is not carried away by any impulse of joy, anger, or fear; such a one is My beloved.
sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः।हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.16 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: He who expects nothing, is pure, watchful, indifferent, unruffled, and renounces all initiative—such a one is My beloved.
sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.17 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: He who is beyond joy and hate, who neither laments nor desires, to whom good and evil fortunes are the same, such a one is beloved to Me.
sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.18 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: He to whom friend and foe are alike, who welcomes equally honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and who is enamored of nothing—
sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.19 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Who is indifferent to praise and censure, enjoys silence, is content with every fate, has no fixed abode, is steadfast in mind, and filled with devotion—such a one is My beloved.
sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 12.20 (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: Verily, those who love the spiritual wisdom as I have taught, whose faith never wavers, and who focus their entire being on Me, they are indeed My most beloved.
sanskrit: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते।श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.1 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, who is God, what is Nature, what is Matter, and what is the Self? What is Wisdom, and what is worth knowing? I wish to have this explained."
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च। / एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.2 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Arjuna! The body of a person is the playground of the Self; and That which knows the activities of Matter, sages call the Self.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते।एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.3 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: I am the omniscient Self that abides in the realm of matter; knowledge of matter and of the all-knowing Self is wisdom.
sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत। / क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.4 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: What is called Matter, of what it is composed, whence it came, and why it changes, what the Self is, and what its power - this I will now briefly set forth.
sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.5 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Seers have sung of it in various ways, in many hymns and sacred Vedic songs, weighty in thought and convincing in their arguments.
sanskrit: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक्।ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.6 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: The five great fundamentals—earth, fire, air, water, and ether—personality, intellect, the mysterious life force, the ten organs of perception and action, the mind, and the five domains of sensation—
sanskrit: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च।इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.7 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, sympathy, vitality, and the persistent clinging to life—these are, in brief, the constituents of changing matter.
sanskrit: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः।एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.8 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Humility, sincerity, harmlessness, forgiveness, rectitude, service to the Master, purity, steadfastness, and self-control;
sanskrit: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम्।आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.9 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Renouncing the delights of the senses, being without pride, having a right understanding of the painful problem of birth and death, and of age and sickness;
sanskrit: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च।जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.10 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Indifference, non-attachment to sex, progeny, or home, equanimity in both good fortune and bad;
sanskrit: असक्ितरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु।नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.11 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Unswerving devotion to Me, with concentration on Me and Me alone, a love for solitude, and indifference to social life;
sanskrit: मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्ितरव्यभिचारिणी।विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.12 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Constant yearning for the knowledge of the Self, and pondering over the lessons of the great Truth—this is wisdom; all else is ignorance.
sanskrit: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोन्यथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.13 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: I will now speak to you of that great truth which one ought to know, since by it one will attain immortal bliss—that which is without beginning, the eternal spirit which dwells in me, neither with form nor without it.
sanskrit: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते।अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.14 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Everywhere are Its hands and feet; everywhere It has eyes that see, heads that think, and mouths that speak; everywhere It listens; It dwells in all the worlds and envelops them all.
sanskrit: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.15 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Beyond the senses, it yet shines through every sense perception; bound to nothing, it yet sustains everything; unaffected by the qualities, it still enjoys them all.
sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.16 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: It is within all beings, yet outside; motionless yet moving; too subtle to be perceived; far away yet ever near.
sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.17 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: In all beings, undivided yet living in division, it is the upholder of all, both creator and destroyer alike.
sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.18 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: It is the light of lights, beyond the reach of darkness; the wisdom, the only thing worth knowing or that wisdom can teach; the presence in the hearts of all.
sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.19 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Thus, I have briefly told you what Matter is, the Self worth realizing, and what Wisdom is. He who is devoted to Me knows, and he will assuredly enter into Me.
sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.20 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
