text: Know further that Nature and God have no beginning, and that differences in character and quality originate from Nature only.
sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.21 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Nature is the law that generates cause and effect; God is the source of all pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.22 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: God, dwelling in the heart of Nature, experiences the qualities that Nature brings forth; and His affinity towards these qualities is the reason for His living in a good or evil body.
sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.23 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Thus, in the body of man dwells the Supreme God; He who sees, permits, upholds, and enjoys is the Highest God and the Highest Self.
sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.24 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: He who understands God and Nature, along with her qualities, whatever his condition in life may be, will not come back to earth.
sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.25 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Some realize the Supreme by meditating, with its aid, on the Self within; others by pure reason; and still others by right action.
sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.26 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Others, again, having no direct knowledge but only hearing from others, still worship, and, if they are true to the teachings, they too will cross the sea of death.
sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते।तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.27 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Wherever life is seen in things movable or immovable, it is the result of the combination of Matter and Spirit.
sanskrit: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.28 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he is the one who truly sees.
sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.29 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Beholding the Lord equally in all things, his actions do not mar his spiritual life but lead him to the heights of bliss.
sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.30 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: He who understands that it is only the Law of Nature that brings action to fruition, and that the Self never acts, alone knows the Truth.
sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.31 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: He who sees the diverse forms of life all rooted in One and growing forth from Him, shall indeed find the Absolute.
sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.32 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: The Supreme Spirit, O Prince, is without beginning, has no qualities, and is imperishable. Though it is within the body, it does not act, nor is it affected by action.
sanskrit: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.33 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: As space, though present everywhere, remains unaffected due to its subtlety, so too the Self, though present in all forms, retains its purity unalloyed.
sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.34 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: As the one Sun illuminates the entire earth, so the Lord illuminates the entire universe.
sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः।क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 13.35 (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: Those who, with the eyes of wisdom, thus see the difference between Matter and Spirit, and know how to liberate life from the Law of Nature, attain the Supreme.
sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा।भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.1 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Lord Shri Krishna continued: Now I will reveal to you the wisdom that is beyond knowledge, by attaining which the sages have reached perfection.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्।यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.2 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Dwelling in wisdom and realizing My divinity, they are not reborn when the universe is recreated at the beginning of every cycle, nor are they affected when it is dissolved.
sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.3 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: The eternal cosmos is My womb, in which I plant the seed from which all beings are born, O prince!
sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम्।संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.4 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: O illustrious son of Kunti! Through whatever wombs men are born, it is the Spirit itself that conceives, and I am their father.
sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.5 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Purity, passion, and ignorance are the qualities that the law of nature brings forth. They fetter the free spirit in all beings.
sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः।निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.6 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: O Sinless One! Of these, purity, being luminous, strong, and invulnerable, binds one with its yearning for happiness and illumination.
sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम्।सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.7 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Passion, engendered by thirst for pleasure and attachment, binds the soul through its fondness for activities.
sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम्।तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.8 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: But Ignorance, the product of darkness, stupefies the senses of all embodied beings, binding them with chains of folly, indolence, and lethargy.
sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम्।प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.9 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Purity brings happiness, passion brings commotion, and ignorance, which obscures wisdom, leads to a life of failure.
sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.10 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: O Prince! Purity prevails when passion and ignorance are overcome; passion, when purity and ignorance are overcome; and ignorance when it is overcome by purity and passion.
sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत।रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.11 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: When the light of knowledge gleams forth from all the gates of the body, then be sure that purity prevails.
sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते।ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.12 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: O best of Indians! Avarice, the impulse to act, and the beginning of action itself are all due to the dominance of passion.
sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.13 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Darkness, stagnation, folly, and infatuation are the results of the dominance of ignorance, O joy of the Kuru clan!
sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च।तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.14 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: When purity prevails, the soul, upon leaving the body, passes on to the pure regions where those who know the Highest reside.
sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.15 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: When passion prevails, the soul is reborn among those who love activity; when ignorance rules, it enters the wombs of the ignorant.
sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते।तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.16 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: They say the fruit of a meritorious action is spotless and pure; the outcome of passion is misery, and of ignorance, darkness.
sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.17 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Purity engenders wisdom, passion avarice, and ignorance folly, infatuation, and darkness.
sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च।प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.18 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: When purity is in the ascendant, the man evolves; when passion is in the ascendant, he neither evolves nor degenerates; when ignorance is in the ascendant, he is lost.
sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.19 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: As soon as one understands that it is only the qualities that act and nothing else, and perceives that which is beyond, they attain My divine nature.
sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.20 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: When the soul transcends the Qualities, which are the real cause of physical existence, then, freed from birth and death, from old age and misery, he drinks the nectar of immortality.
sanskrit: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान्।जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.21 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, how can one recognize someone who has transcended the qualities? How do they act and live beyond them?"
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.22 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Prince! He who does not shun the quality that is present and does not long for that which is absent;
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.23 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: He who maintains an attitude of indifference, who is not disturbed by the qualities, who realizes that it is only they who act, and remains calm;
sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.24 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Who accepts pain and pleasure as they come, is centered in their Self, to whom a piece of clay, stone, or gold are all the same, who neither likes nor dislikes, who is steadfast, indifferent alike to praise or censure;
sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.25 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: Who looks equally upon honor and dishonor, loves friends and foes alike, and abandons all initiative, such is he who transcends the qualities.
sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.26 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: And he who serves Me alone, with unwavering devotion, shall overcome the Qualities and become one with the Eternal.
sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते।स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते

source: Bhagavad Gita 14.27 (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: For I am the home of the spirit, the continual source of immortality, eternal righteousness, and infinite joy.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च।शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.1 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Lord Shri Krishna continued: This phenomenal creation, which is both ephemeral and eternal, is like a tree, with its seed above in the Highest and its ramifications below on this earth. The scriptures are its leaves, and he who understands this knows.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.2 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Its branches shoot upwards and downwards, deriving their nourishment from the qualities; its buds are the objects of sense; and its roots, which follow the law, causing man's regeneration and degeneration, pierce downwards into the soil.
sanskrit: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः।अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.3 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: In this world, its true form is not known, neither its origin nor its end, and its strength is not understood—until the tree, with its roots striking deep into the earth, is hewn down by the sharp axe of non-attachment.
sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा।अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.4 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Beyond lies the path, from which, once found, there is no return. This is the Primal God from whom this ancient creation has sprung.
sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.5 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: The wise attain Eternity when, freed from pride and delusion, they have conquered their love for the things of sense; when, renouncing desire and fixing their gaze on the Self, they cease to be tossed to and fro by the opposing sensations, such as pleasure and pain.
sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः।द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.6 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!
sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.7 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: It is only a very small part of My Eternal Self, which is the life of the universe, that draws around itself the six senses, with the mind being the last, which have their source in Nature.
sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः।मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.8 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: When the Supreme Lord enters a body or leaves it, He gathers these senses together and travels with them, as the wind gathers perfume while passing through the flowers.
sanskrit: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः।गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.9 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: He is the perception of the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste, the smell, and the mind; and the enjoyment of the things they perceive is also His.
sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च।अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.10 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: The ignorant do not see that it is He who is present in life and departs at death, or even that it is He who enjoys pleasure through the qualities. Only the eye of wisdom sees this.
sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्।विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.11 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: The saints, with great effort, find Him within themselves; however, the unintelligent, despite their efforts, cannot control their minds.
sanskrit: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम्।यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.12 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Remember that the light which proceeds from the sun, illuminating the whole world, and the light which is in the moon, and that which is in the fire, all are born of me.
sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्।यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.13 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: I enter this world and animate all My creatures with My vitality; and by My cool moonbeams, I nourish the plants.
sanskrit: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा।पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.14 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Becoming the fire of life, I pass into their bodies and, uniting with the vital streams of Prāṇa and Apāna, I digest the various kinds of food.
sanskrit: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः।प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.15 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: I am enthroned in the hearts of all; memory, wisdom, and discrimination owe their origins to Me. I am He Who is to be realized in the scriptures; I inspire their wisdom, and I know their truth.
sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च।वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.16 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: There are two aspects in Nature: the perishable and the imperishable. All life in this world belongs to the former, while the unchanging element belongs to the latter.
sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.17 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: But I am higher than all, the Supreme God, the Absolute Self, the Eternal Lord, who pervades and upholds all the worlds.
sanskrit: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः।यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.18 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: I am beyond comparison with the Eternal and the non-eternal; I am known as the Supreme Personality, the Highest God, by scriptures and sages.
sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.19 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: He who, with unclouded vision, sees Me as the Lord-God, knows all that there is to be known and will always worship Me with his whole heart.
sanskrit: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 15.20 (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: Thus, O sinless one, I have revealed this most mystic knowledge to thee. He who understands it gains wisdom and attains the consummation of life.
sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ।एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.1 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Lord Shri Krishna continued: Fearlessness, clean living, unceasing concentration on wisdom, readiness to give, self-control, a spirit of sacrifice, regular study of the scriptures, austerity, candor,
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः। / दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.2 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, contentment, straightforwardness, compassion towards all, uncovetousness, courtesy, modesty, and constancy.
sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम्।दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.3 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Valor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from hate and vanity—these are the qualities of one who possesses the divine, O Arjuna!
sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता। / भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.4 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Hypocrisy, pride, insolence, cruelty, and ignorance belong to those born of godless qualities.
sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च।अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.5 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless ones lead to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! You have the Godly qualities.
sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता।मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.6 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: No changes needed.
sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.7 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: The godless do not know how to act or renounce; they lack both purity and truth. They do not understand the right principles of conduct.
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः।न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.8 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: They say the universe is an accident with no purpose and no God. Life is created through sexual union, a product of lust and nothing else.
sanskrit: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम्।अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.9 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Thinking thus, these degraded souls, these enemies of mankind—whose intelligence is negligible and whose deeds are monstrous—come into the world only to destroy.
sanskrit: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः।प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.10 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Giving themselves up to insatiable passions, hypocritically, self-sufficiently, and arrogantly, cherishing false conceptions founded on delusion, they work only to carry out their own unholy purposes.
sanskrit: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः।मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.11 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Poring anxiously over evil resolutions that only end in death, seeking only the gratification of desire as the highest goal, and seeing nothing beyond—
sanskrit: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः।कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.12 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Caught in the toils of a hundred vain hopes, enslaved by passion and wrath, they accumulate hoards of unjust wealth, only to indulge their sensual desires.
sanskrit: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः।ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.13 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Today I have gained this; tomorrow I will fulfill another desire; this wealth is mine now, and the rest will soon be mine.
sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम्।इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.14 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: I have slain one enemy; I will slay the others too. I am worthy of enjoying; I am the Almighty, perfect, powerful, and happy.
sanskrit: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि।ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.15 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: I am wealthy, I am of noble birth; who can compare with me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will pay—and I will enjoy. Thus blinded by ignorance,
sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया।यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.16 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Perplexed by discordant thoughts, entangled in the snares of desire, infatuated by passion, they sink into the depths of hell.
sanskrit: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः।प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.17 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Self-conceited, stubborn, wealthy, proud, and insolent, they make a show of their patronage, disregarding the norms of propriety.
sanskrit: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.18 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Puffed up by power and inordinate conceit, swayed by lust and wrath, these wicked people hate Me, Who am within them as I am within all.
sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.19 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Those who thus hate Me, who are cruel, the dregs of mankind, I condemn them to a continuous, miserable, and godless rebirth.
sanskrit: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान्।क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.20 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: So, reborn, they spend life after life enveloped in delusion, and they never reach Me, O Prince, but degenerate into even lower forms of life.
sanskrit: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.21 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.
sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.22 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: These are the gates that lead to darkness; if one avoids them, they will ensure their own welfare and eventually attain liberation.
sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः।आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.23 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: But he who neglects the commands of the scriptures and follows the promptings of passion does not attain perfection, happiness, or the final goal.
sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 16.24 (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: Therefore, whenever there is doubt as to whether you should do something or not, let the scriptures guide your conduct. In the light of the scriptures, you should labor your whole life.
sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.1 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is the condition of those who perform acts of sacrifice not according to the scriptures, but with implicit faith? Is it one of purity, passion, or ignorance?"
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.2 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Man has an inherent faith in one or another of the qualities—purity, passion, and ignorance. Now, listen.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.3 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.
sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.4 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The pure worship the true God; the passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the ignorant, the spirits of the dead and lower orders of nature.
sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.5 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Those who practice austerities not commanded by scripture, who are enslaved to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,
sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.6 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: They are ignorant and torment the organs of the body, harassing Me who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.
sanskrit: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः।मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.7 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The food that people enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.
sanskrit: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.8 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The foods that prolong life, increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness, and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial, and agreeable; these are loved by the pure.
sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः।रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.9 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Those in whom passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance, and disease.
sanskrit: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.10 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The ignorant love food that is stale, not nourishing, putrid, and corrupt; the leftovers of others, and unclean.
sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.11 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Sacrifice is pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit of it, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.
sanskrit: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.12 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of passion.
sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.13 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith—that is the product of ignorance.
sanskrit: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्।श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.14 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence, and harmlessness—all of these constitute physical austerity.
sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.15 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.
sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.16 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity—these are the austerities of the mind.
sanskrit: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.17 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: These threefold austerities, performed with faith and without thought of reward, can truly be considered pure.
sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.18 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Austerity coupled with hypocrisy, or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity, or vanity, comes from passion, and its result is always uncertain and temporary.
sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.19 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or the infliction of pain upon oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from ignorance.
sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.20 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The gift that is given without thought of recompense, believing it should be made, in an appropriate place, at an opportune time, and to a deserving person—such a gift is pure.
sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.21 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense, or grudgingly—that may truly be said to be the outcome of passion.
sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.22 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: And that which is given at an inappropriate place or time or to one who is undeserving, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of ignorance.
sanskrit: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते।असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.23 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which the Vedic Scriptures, ceremonials, and sacrifices were ordained of old.
sanskrit: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.24 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Therefore, all acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities prescribed by the scriptures are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word "Om."
sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.25 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity, or gift with the word "Tat" (meaning "That"), without thought of reward.
sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.26 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to denote an action of exceptional merit.
sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.27 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Conviction in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called Sat. So too, an action done only for the Lord's sake.
sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते

source: Bhagavad Gita 17.28 (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: Whatever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity, gift, or anything else, is called Asat (meaning "Unreal"), for it is the negation of Sat, O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter.
sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.1 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Arjuna asked, "O Mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच / संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्। / त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.2 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाच / काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः। / सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.3 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Some philosophers say that all action is evil and should be abandoned, whereas others maintain that acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up.
sanskrit: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। / यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.4 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment regarding this problem. It has a threefold aspect.
sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.5 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up, but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.
sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.6 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But they should be done with detachment and without thought of reward. This is my final judgement.
sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.7 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: It is not right to give up actions which are obligatory; and if they are misunderstood, it is the result of sheer ignorance.
sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते।मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.8 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: To avoid an action out of fear of physical suffering, as it is likely to be painful, is to act out of passion, and the benefit of renunciation will not be gained.
sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत्।स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.9 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: He who performs an obligatory action, believing it to be a duty that ought to be done, without any personal desire to do the act or to receive any return—such renunciation is pure.
sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.10 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The wise man who has attained purity, whose doubts are resolved, who is filled with the spirit of self-abnegation, does not shy away from action due to its pain, nor does he crave it due to its pleasure.
sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते।त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.11 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But since those still in the body cannot entirely avoid action, in their case, the abandonment of the fruit of action is considered as complete renunciation.
sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.12 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: For those who cannot renounce all desires, the fruit of action hereafter is threefold—good, evil, and partly good and partly evil. But for him who has renounced, there is none.
sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.13 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: I will now tell you, O Mighty Man, the five causes that must come together, according to the final decision of philosophy, for an action to be accomplished.
sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.14 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: They have a body, a personality, physical organs, and manifold activities and destinies.
sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.15 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Whatever action a person performs, whether by muscular effort, speech, or thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.
sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः।न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.16 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But the fool, who, due to his immature judgment, supposes that it is his own Self alone that acts, perverts the truth and does not see rightly.
sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.17 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: He who has no pride and whose intellect is unalloyed by attachment, even though he kills these people, he does not kill them, and his act does not bind him.
sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.18 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge are the three incentives to action; and the act, the actor, and the instrument are the threefold constituents.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.19 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The knowledge, the action, and the doer differ according to their qualities. Listen to this as well.
sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.20 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, can be truly called Pure Knowledge.
sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते।अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.21 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The knowledge that perceives the manifold existence in all beings as separate comes from passion.
sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान्।वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.22 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth, or insight, has its origin in darkness.
sanskrit: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम्।अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.23 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that may follow, such an action is Pure.
sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम्।अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.24 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But even though an action involves the most strenuous endeavor, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify their desires and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in passion.
sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.25 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: An action undertaken through delusion, with no regard to the spiritual implications, the capacity of the doer, or the potential harm that may follow, is assumed to be a product of ignorance.
sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम्।मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.26 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But when a person has no sentiment or ego, when they possess courage and confidence, not caring whether they succeed or fail, then their action arises from purity.
sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.27 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: In one who is impulsive, greedy, looking for reward, violent, impure, and torn between joy and sorrow, it may be assumed that Passion is predominant.
sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः।हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.28 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: While he whose purpose is weak, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—he may be assumed to be in darkness.
sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः।विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.29 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the quality that is dominant. I will explain them fully and separately, O Arjuna!
sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु।प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.30 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is Pure.
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.31 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The intellect that does not understand what is right and wrong, and what should be done and not done, is under the sway of Passion.
sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.32 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong to be right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.
sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता।सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.33 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The conviction and steady concentration with which the mind, the energy, and the senses are controlled—O Arjuna!—are the result of purity.
sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.34 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The conviction that always holds fast to rituals, self-interest, and wealth for the sake of what they may bring forth comes from passion.
sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन।प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.35 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: And that which clings perversely to false idealism, fear, grief, despair, and vanity is the product of ignorance.
sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.36 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Hear further the three kinds of pleasure. That which increases day by day delivers one from misery.
sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.37 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Which at first seems like poison but afterwards acts like nectar—that pleasure is pure, for it is born of wisdom.
sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम्।तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.38 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: That which, at first, is like nectar, as the senses revel in their objects, but in the end acts like poison—that pleasure arises from Passion.
sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम्।परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.39 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: While the pleasure that drugs the senses from start to finish, which springs from indolence, lethargy, and folly—that pleasure flows from Ignorance.
sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः।निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.40 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: There is nothing anywhere on earth or in the higher worlds that is free from the three Qualities, for they are born of Nature.
sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.41 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: O Arjuna! The duties of spiritual teachers, the soldiers, the traders, and the servants have all been fixed according to the dominant quality in their nature.
sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप।कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.42 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, uprightness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in God—these constitute the duty of a spiritual teacher.
sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च।ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.43 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Valor, glory, firmness, skill, generosity, steadiness in battle, and the ability to rule—these constitute the duty of a soldier. They flow from his own nature.
sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम्।दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.44 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Agriculture, the protection of cows, and trade are the duties of a trader, in accordance with his nature. The duty of a servant is to serve, which also agrees with his nature.
sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम्।परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.45 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Perfection is attained when one diligently attends to their duty. Listen, and I will tell you how it is attained by one who always minds their own duty.
sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.46 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: One reaches perfection by dedicating their actions to God, Who is the source of all being and fills everything.
sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.47 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: It is better to do one's own duty, however defective it may be, than to follow the duty of another, however well one may perform it. He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never commits a sin.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.48 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The duty that falls to one's lot of its own accord should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, just as fire is obscured by smoke.
sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.49 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: He whose mind is entirely detached, who has conquered himself, and whose desires have vanished, reaches that stage of perfect freedom through his renunciation, where action completes itself and leaves no seed.
sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः।नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.50 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: I will now state briefly how one who has reached perfection finds the Eternal Spirit, the state of Supreme Wisdom.
sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.51 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Guided always by pure reason, bravely restraining himself, renouncing the objects of sense and giving up attachment and hatred; he attains peace.
sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च।शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.52 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Enjoying solitude, being abstemious, having his body, mind, and speech under perfect control, and being absorbed in meditation, he becomes free—always filled with the spirit of renunciation.
sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः।ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.53 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Having abandoned selfishness, power, arrogance, anger, and desire, possessing nothing of his own, and having attained peace, he is fit to join the Eternal Spirit.
sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.54 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: When he unites with the Eternal and his soul knows the bliss of the Self, he feels no desire or regret, he regards all beings equally, and enjoys the blessing of supreme devotion to Me.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.55 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: By such devotion, he sees Me, who I am and what I am; and thus realizing the truth, he enters into My kingdom.
sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः।ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.56 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Relying on Me in all his actions and doing them for My sake, he attains, by My grace, eternal and unchangeable life.
sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.57 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Surrender your actions to Me, live in Me, focus your intellect on Me, and always think of Me.
sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः।बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.58 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Fix your mind on Me, and by My grace you will overcome the obstacles in your path. But if, misled by pride, you do not listen, then you will indeed be lost.
sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि।अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.59 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: If you in your vanity think of avoiding this fight, your will shall not be fulfilled, for Nature herself will compel you.
sanskrit: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे।मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.60 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: O Arjuna! Your duty binds you. It has arisen from your own nature, and that which you do not desire to do in your delusion, you will do that very thing. You are helpless.
sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा।कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.61 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: God dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna! He causes them to revolve, as it were, on a wheel, by His mystic power.
sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.62 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: With all your strength, fly to Him and surrender yourself, and by His grace you will attain Supreme Peace and reach the Eternal Home.
sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.63 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.
sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.64 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Listen to My last word once more, the deepest secret of all; you are My beloved, you are My friend, and I speak for your welfare.
sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.65 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Dedicate yourself to Me, worship Me, sacrifice all for Me, prostrate yourself before Me, and you will surely come to Me. I truly pledge to you; you are My beloved.
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.66 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.
sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.67 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Do not speak this to one who has not practiced austerities, or to one who does not love, or who will not listen, or who mocks.
sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन।न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.68 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: But he who teaches this great secret to My devotees, his is the highest devotion, and he shall surely come to Me.
sanskrit: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.69 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: There is no one among men who can perform a service dearer to Me than this, nor is there any man on earth more beloved by Me than him.
sanskrit: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः।भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.70 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: He who will study this spiritual discourse of ours, I assure you, they shall thereby worship Me at the altar of Wisdom.
sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.71 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Yes, he who listens to it with faith and without doubt, even he, freed from evil, will rise to the worlds which the virtuous attain through righteous deeds.
sanskrit: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः।सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.72 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: O Arjuna, have you listened attentively to My words? Has your ignorance and delusion gone?
sanskrit: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा।कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.73 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Arjuna replied: "My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Your Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts have been dispelled, and I stand before You ready to do Your will."
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत।स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.74 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Sanjaya said: "I heard this rare, wonderful, and soul-stirring discourse between Lord Shri Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna.
sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः।संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.75 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Through the blessing of the sage Vyasa, I heard this secret and noble science from the lips of its Master, Lord Shri Krishna.
sanskrit: व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम्।योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.76 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: O King! The more I think of that marvelous and holy discourse, the more I lose myself in joy.
sanskrit: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम्।केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.77 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: As I recall again and again the exceeding beauty of the Lord, I am filled with amazement and joy.
sanskrit: तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः। / विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः

source: Bhagavad Gita 18.78 (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.
sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः। / तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम।।18.78।

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 1 summary (Arjuna's Dilemma)
text: The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita - "Arjuna Vishada Yoga" introduces the setup, the setting, the characters and the circumstances that led to the epic battle of Mahabharata, fought between the Pandavas and the Kauravas. It outlines the reasons that led to the revelation of the of Bhagavad Gita. As both armies stand ready for the battle, the mighty warrior Arjuna, on observing the warriors on both sides becomes increasingly sad and depressed due to the fear of losing his relatives and friends and the consequent sins attributed to killing his own relatives. So, he surrenders to Lord Krishna, seeking a solution. Thus, follows the wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 2 summary (Transcendental Knowledge)
text: The second chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sankhya Yoga". This is the most important chapter of the Bhagavad Gita as Lord Krishna condenses the teachings of the entire Gita in this chapter. This chapter is the essence of the entire Gita. "Sankhya Yoga" can be categorized into 4 main topics - 1. Arjuna completely surrenders himself to Lord Krishna and accepts his position as a disciple and Krishna as his Guru. He requests Krishna to guide him on how to dismiss his sorrow. 2. Explanation of the main cause of all grief, which is ignorance of the true nature of Self. 3. Karma Yoga - the discipline of selfless action without being attached to its fruits. 4. Description of a Perfect Man - One whose mind is steady and one-pointed.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 3 summary (Path of Selfless Service)
text: The third chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Yoga" or the "Path of Selfless Service". Here Lord Krishna emphasizes the importance of karma in life. He reveals that it is important for every human being to engage in some sort of activity in this material world. Further, he describes the kinds of actions that lead to bondage and the kinds that lead to liberation. Those persons who continue to perform their respective duties externally for the pleasure of the Supreme, without attachment to its rewards get liberation at the end.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 4 summary (Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action)
text: The fourth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna glorifies the Karma Yoga and imparts the Transcendental Knowledge (the knowledge of the soul and the Ultimate Truth) to Arjuna. He reveals the reason behind his appearance in this material world. He reveals that even though he is eternal, he reincarnates time after time to re-establish dharma and peace on this Earth. His births and activities are eternal and are never contaminated by material flaws. Those persons who know and understand this Truth engage in his devotion with full faith and eventually attain Him. They do not have to take birth in this world again.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 5 summary (Path of Renunciation)
text: The fifth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna compares the paths of renunciation in actions (Karma Sanyas) and actions with detachment (Karma Yoga) and explains that both are means to reach the same goal and we can choose either. A wise person should perform his/her worldly duties without attachment to the fruits of his/her actions and dedicate them to God. This way they remain unaffected by sin and eventually attain liberation.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 6 summary (Path of Meditation)
text: The sixth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Dhyana Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the "Yoga of Meditation" and how to practise this Yoga. He discusses the role of action in preparing for Meditation, how performing duties in devotion purifies one's mind and heightens one's spiritual consciousness. He explains in detail the obstacles that one faces when trying to control their mind and the exact methods by which one can conquer their mind. He reveals how one can focus their mind on Paramatma and unite with the God.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 7 summary (Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment)
text: The seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gyaan Vigyana Yoga ". In this chapter, Krishna reveals that he is the Supreme Truth, the principal cause and the sustaining force of everything. He reveals his illusionary energy in this material world called Maya, which is very difficult to overcome but those who surrender their minds unto Him attain Him easily. He also describes the four types of people who surrender to Him in devotion and the four kinds that don't. Krishna confirms that He is the Ultimate Reality and those who realize this Truth reach the pinnacle of spiritual realization and unite with the Lord.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 8 summary (Path of the Eternal God)
text: The eighth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Akshara Brahma Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the importance of the last thought before death. If we can remember Krishna at the time of death, we will certainly attain him. Thus, it is very important to be in constant awareness of the Lord at all times, thinking of Him and chanting His names at all times. By perfectly absorbing their mind in Him through constant devotion, one can go beyond this material existence to Lord's Supreme abode.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 9 summary (Yoga through the King of Sciences)
text: The ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Raja Vidya Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna explains that He is Supreme and how this material existence is created, maintained and destroyed by His Yogmaya and all beings come and go under his supervision. He reveals the Role and the Importance of Bhakti (transcendental devotional service) towards our Spiritual Awakening. In such devotion, one must live for the God, offer everything that he possesses to Him and do everything for Him only. One who follows such devotion becomes free from the bonds of this material world and unites with the Lord.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 10 summary (Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God)
text: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vibhooti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals Himself as the cause of all causes. He describes His various manifestations and opulences in order to increase Arjuna's Bhakti. Arjuna is fully convinced of Lord's paramount position and proclaims him to be the Supreme Personality. He prays to Krishna to describe more of His divine glories which are like nectar to hear.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 11 summary (Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God)
text: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga". In this chapter, Arjuna requests Krishna to reveal His Universal Cosmic Form that encompasses all the universes, the entire existence. Arjuna is granted divine vision to be able to see the entirety of creation in the body of the Supreme Lord Krishna.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 12 summary (The Yoga of Devotion)
text: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Bhakti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna emphasizes the superiority of Bhakti Yoga (the path of devotion) over all other types of spiritual disciplines and reveals various aspects of devotion. He further explains that the devotees who perform pure devotional service to Him, with their consciousness, merged in Him and all their actions dedicated to Him, are quickly liberated from the cycle of life and death. He also describes the various qualities of the devotees who are very dear to Him.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 13 summary (Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field)
text: The thirteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga". The word "kshetra" means "the field", and the "kshetrajna" means "the knower of the field". We can think of our material body as the field and our immortal soul as the knower of the field. In this chapter, Krishna discriminates between the physical body and the immortal soul. He explains that the physical body is temporary and perishable whereas the soul is permanent and eternal. The physical body can be destroyed but the soul can never be destroyed. The chapter then describes God, who is the Supreme Soul. All the individual souls have originated from the Supreme Soul. One who clearly understands the difference between the body, the Soul and the Supreme Soul attains the realization of Brahman.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 14 summary (Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature)
text: The fourteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the three gunas (modes) of the material nature - goodness, passion and ignorance which everything in the material existence is influenced by. He further explains the essential characteristics of each of these modes, their cause and how they influence a living entity affected by them. He then reveals the various characteristics of the persons who have gone beyond these gunas. The chapter ends with Krishna reminding us of the power of pure devotion to God and how attachment to God can help us transcend these gunas.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 15 summary (The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality)
text: The fifteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Purushottama Yoga". In Sanskrit, Purusha means the "All-pervading God", and Purushottam means the timeless & transcendental aspect of God. Krishna reveals that the purpose of this Transcendental knowledge of the God is to detach ourselves from the bondage of the material world and to understand Krishna as the Supreme Divine Personality, who is the eternal controller and sustainer of the world. One who understands this Ultimate Truth surrenders to Him and engages in His devotional service.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 16 summary (Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures)
text: The sixteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes explicitly the two kinds of natures among human beings - divine and demoniac. Those who possess demonaic qualities associate themselves with the modes of passion and ignorance do not follow the regulations of the scriptures and embrace materialistic views. These people attain lower births and further material bondage. But people who possess divine qualities, follow the instructions of the scriptures, associate themselves with the mode of goodness and purify the mind through spiritual practices. This leads to the enhancement of divine qualities and they eventually attain spiritual realization.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 17 summary (Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith)
text: The seventeenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes the three types of faith corresponding to the three modes of the material nature. Lord Krishna further reveals that it is the nature of faith that determines the quality of life and the character of living entities. Those who have faith in passion and ignorance perform actions that yield temporary, material results while those who have faith in goodness perform actions in accordance with scriptural instructions and hence their hearts get further purified.

source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 18 summary (Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender)
text: The eighteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Moksha Sanyas Yoga". Arjuna requests the Lord to explain the difference between the two types of renunciations - sanyaas(renunciation of actions) and tyaag(renunciation of desires). Krishna explains that a sanyaasi is one who abandons family and society in order to practise spiritual discipline whereas a tyaagi is one who performs their duties without attachment to the rewards of their actions and dedicating them to the God. Krishna recommends the second kind of renunciation - tyaag. Krishna then gives a detailed analysis of the effects of the three modes of material nature. He declares that the highest path of spirituality is pure, unconditional loving service unto the Supreme Divine Personality, Krishna. If we always remember Him, keep chanting His name and dedicate all our actions unto Him, take refuge in Him and make Him our Supreme goal, then by His grace, we will surely overcome all obstacles and difficulties and be freed from this cycle of birth and death.

source: Vishnu Purana, Book V (tr. Wilson, 1840): The Vishnu Purana, Book V, Chapter 1
text:
**Summary.** The death of Kansa announced. Earth, oppressed by the Daityas, applies to the gods. They accompany her to Vishńu, who promises to give her relief. Kansa imprisons Vasudeva and Devakí. Vishńu's instructions to Yoganidrá.

MAITREYA.--You have related to me a full account of all the different dynasties of kings, and of their successive transactions. I wish now to hear a more particular description, holy Rishi, of the portion of Vishńu that came down upon earth, and was born in the family of Yadu. Tell me also what actions he performed in his descent, as a part of a part of the supreme, upon the earth.

PARÁŚARA.--I will relate to you, Maitreya, the account which you have requested; the birth of a part of a part of Vishńu, and the benefits which his actions conferred upon the world.

source: Vishnu Purana, Book V (tr. Wilson, 1840): The Vishnu Purana, Book V, Chapter 1
text: Vasudeva formerly married the daughter of Devaka, the illustrious Devakí, a maiden of celestial beauty. After their nuptials, Kansa, the increaser of the race of Bhoja, drove their car as their charioteer. As they were going along, a voice in the sky, sounding aloud and deep as thunder, addressed Kansa, and said, "Fool that you are, the eighth child of the damsel whom you are driving in the car shall take away your life!" On hearing this, Kansa drew his sword, and was about to put Devakí to death; but Vasudeva interposed, saying, "Kill not Devakí, great warrior; spare her life, and I will deliver to you every child that she may bring forth." Appeased by which promise, and relying on the character of Vasudeva, Kansa desisted from the attempt.

source: Vishnu Purana, Book V (tr. Wilson, 1840): The Vishnu Purana, Book V, Chapter 1
text: At that time, Earth, overburdened by her load, repaired to mount Meru to an assembly of the gods, and addressing the divinities, with Brahmá at their head, related in piteous accents all her distress. "Agni," said Earth, "is the progenitor of gold; Súrya, of rays of light: the parent and guide of me and of all spheres is the supreme Náráyańa, who is Brahmá, the lord of the lord of patriarchs; the eldest of the eldest born; one with minutes and hours; one with time; having form, though indiscrete. This assemblage of yourselves, O gods, is but a part of him. The sun, the winds, the saints, the Rudras, the Vasus, the Aswins, fire, the patriarch creators of the universe, of whom Atri is the first, all are but forms of the mighty and inscrutable Vishńu. The Yakshas, Rákshasas, Daityas, spirits of evil, serpents, and children of Danu, the singers and nymphs of heaven, are forms of the great spirit, Vishńu. The heavens painted with planets, constellations, and stars; fire, water, wind, and myself, and every perceptible thing; the whole universe itself--consists of Vishńu.

source: Vishnu Purana, Book V (tr. Wilson, 1840): The Vishnu Purana, Book V, Chapter 1
text: The multifarious forms of that manifold being encounter and succeed one another, night and day, like the waves of the sea. At this present season many demons, of whom Kálanemi is the chief, have overrun, and continually harrass, the region of mortals. The great Asura Kálanemi, that was killed by the powerful Vishńu, has revived in Kansa, the son of Ugrasena, and many other mighty demons, more than I can enumerate, as Arisht́a, Dhenuka, Keśin, Pralamba, Naraka, Sunda, and the fierce Báńa, the son of Bali, are born in the palaces of kings.
